Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SimpleDefinitionFinder.getSimplifiedName(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SimpleDefinitionFinder.java
Original range: 137-149
Documentation:
/**
   * Extract a name from a node.  In the case of GETPROP nodes,
   * replace the namespace or object expression with "this" for
   * simplicity and correctness at the expense of inefficiencies due
   * to higher chances of name collisions.
   *
   * TODO(user) revisit.  it would be helpful to at least use fully
   * qualified names in the case of namespaces.  Might not matter as
   * much if this pass runs after "collapsing properties".
   */
Method code:
137 |   private static String getSimplifiedName(Node node) {
138 |     if (NodeUtil.isName(node)) {
139 |       String name = node.getString();
140 |       if (name != null && !name.isEmpty()) {
141 |         return name;
142 |       } else {
143 |         return null;
144 |       }
145 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isGetProp(node)) {
146 |       return "this." + node.getLastChild().getString();
147 |     }
148 |     return null;
149 |   }

===== M0012 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.java
Original range: 64-96
Documentation:

Method code:
64 |   @Override
65 |   public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
66 |     Node declarationRoot = t.getScopeRoot();
67 |     Renamer renamer;
68 |     if (nameStack.isEmpty()) {
69 |       // If the contextual renamer is being used the starting context can not
70 |       // be a function.
71 |       Preconditions.checkState(
72 |           declarationRoot.getType() != Token.FUNCTION ||
73 |           !(rootRenamer instanceof ContextualRenamer));
74 |       Preconditions.checkState(t.inGlobalScope());
75 |       renamer = rootRenamer;
76 |     } else {
77 |       renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
78 |     }
79 | 
80 |     if (declarationRoot.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
81 |       // Add the function parameters
82 |       Node fnParams = declarationRoot.getFirstChild().getNext();
83 |       for (Node c = fnParams.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
84 |         String name = c.getString();
85 |         renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
86 |       }
87 | 
88 |       // Add the function body declarations
89 |       Node functionBody = declarationRoot.getLastChild();
90 |       findDeclaredNames(functionBody, null, renamer);
91 |     } else {
92 |       // Add the block declarations
93 |       findDeclaredNames(declarationRoot, null, renamer);
94 |     }
95 |     nameStack.push(renamer);
96 |   }

===== M0020 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.StatementFusion.canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/StatementFusion.java
Original range: 46-83
Documentation:

Method code:
46 |   private static boolean canFuseIntoOneStatement(Node block) {
47 |     // Fold only statement block. NOT scripts block.
48 |     if (block.getType() != Token.BLOCK) {
49 |       return false;
50 |     }
51 | 
52 |     // Nothing to do here.
53 |     if (!block.hasChildren() || block.hasOneChild()) {
54 |       return false;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     Node last = block.getLastChild();
58 | 
59 |     for (Node c = block.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
60 |       if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(c) && c != last) {
61 |         return false;
62 |       }
63 |     }
64 | 
65 |     // TODO(user): Support more control statement for fusion.
66 |     // FOR
67 |     switch(last.getType()) {
68 |       case Token.IF:
69 |       case Token.THROW:
70 |       case Token.SWITCH:
71 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
72 |         return true;
73 |       case Token.RETURN:
74 |         // We don't want to add a new return value.
75 |         return last.hasChildren();
76 |       case Token.FOR:
77 |         return NodeUtil.isForIn(last) &&
78 |             // Avoid cases where we have for(var x = foo() in a) { ....
79 |             !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(last.getFirstChild());
80 |     }
81 | 
82 |     return false;
83 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Reports errors for any invalid use of control structures.
   *
   * @param node Current node to check.
   */
Method code:
54 |   private void check(Node node) {
55 |     switch (node.getType()) {
56 |       case Token.WITH:
57 |         JSDocInfo info = node.getJSDocInfo();
58 |         boolean allowWith =
59 |             info != null && info.getSuppressions().contains("with");
60 |         if (!allowWith) {
61 |           report(node, USE_OF_WITH);
62 |         }
63 |         break;
64 |     }
65 | 
66 |     for (Node bChild = node.getFirstChild(); bChild != null;) {
67 |       Node next = bChild.getNext();
68 |       check(bChild);
69 |       bChild = next;
70 |     }
71 |   }

/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
113 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
114 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
115 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
116 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
117 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
118 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
119 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
120 | 
121 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
122 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
123 |         }
124 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
125 |       } else {
126 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
127 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
128 |       }
129 |     }
130 | 
131 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
132 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
133 |     }
134 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)

Original range: 95-156
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
95 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
96 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
97 |     // just bail out early here.
98 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
99 |       return this;
100 |     }
101 | 
102 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
103 | 
104 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
105 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
106 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
107 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
108 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
109 |     }
110 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
111 |       if (alternate instanceof UnionType) {
112 |         UnionType union = (UnionType) alternate;
113 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
114 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
115 |         }
116 |       } else {
117 |         if (alternates.size() > MAX_UNION_SIZE) {
118 |           return this;
119 |         }
120 | 
121 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
122 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
123 |         // one another.
124 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
125 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
126 |           JSType current = it.next();
127 | 
128 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
129 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
130 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
131 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
132 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
133 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
134 |               current.isNoResolvedType()) {
135 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
136 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
137 |               return this;
138 |             }
139 |           } else {
140 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
141 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
142 |               return this;
143 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
144 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
145 |               it.remove();
146 |             }
147 |           }
148 |         }
149 |         alternates.add(alternate);
150 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
151 |       }
152 |     } else {
153 |       result = null;
154 |     }
155 |     return this;
156 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.optimizeSubtree(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeCollectPropertyAssignments.java

34 |   @Override
35 |   Node optimizeSubtree(Node subtree) {
36 |     if (subtree.getType() != Token.SCRIPT
37 |         && subtree.getType() != Token.BLOCK) {
38 |       return subtree;
39 |     }
40 | 
41 |     boolean codeChanged = false;
42 | 
43 |     // Look for variable declarations or simple assignments
44 |     // and start processing there.
45 |     for (Node child = subtree.getFirstChild();
46 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
47 |       if (child.getType() != Token.VAR && !NodeUtil.isExprAssign(child)) {
48 |         continue;
49 |       }
50 |       if (!isPropertyAssignmentToName(child.getNext())) {
51 |         // Quick check to see if there's anything to collapse.
52 |         continue;
53 |       }
54 | 
55 |       Preconditions.checkState(child.hasOneChild());
56 |       Node name = getName(child);
57 |       if (name.getType() != Token.NAME) {
58 |         // The assignment target is not a simple name.
59 |         continue;
60 |       }
61 |       Node value = getValue(child);
62 |       if (value == null || !isInterestingValue(value)) {
63 |         // No initializer or not an Object or Array literal.
64 |         continue;
65 |       }
66 | 
67 |       Node propertyCandidate;
68 |       while ((propertyCandidate = child.getNext()) != null) {
69 |         // This does not infinitely loop because collectProperty always
70 |         // removes propertyCandidate from its parent when it returns true.
71 |         if (!collectProperty(propertyCandidate, name.getString(), value)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |         codeChanged = true;
75 |       }
76 |     }
77 | 
78 |     if (codeChanged) {
79 |       reportCodeChange();
80 |     }
81 |     return subtree;
82 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.strEscape(String,char,String,String,String,CharsetEncoder)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1005-1075
Documentation:
/** Helper to escape javascript string as well as regular expression */
Method code:
1005 |   static String strEscape(String s, char quote,
1006 |                           String doublequoteEscape,
1007 |                           String singlequoteEscape,
1008 |                           String backslashEscape,
1009 |                           CharsetEncoder outputCharsetEncoder) {
1010 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(s.length() + 2);
1011 |     sb.append(quote);
1012 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1013 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1014 |       switch (c) {
1015 |         case '\0': sb.append("\\x00"); break;
1016 |         case '\n': sb.append("\\n"); break;
1017 |         case '\r': sb.append("\\r"); break;
1018 |         case '\t': sb.append("\\t"); break;
1019 |         case '\\': sb.append(backslashEscape); break;
1020 |         case '\"': sb.append(doublequoteEscape); break;
1021 |         case '\'': sb.append(singlequoteEscape); break;
1022 |         case '>':                       // Break --> into --\> or ]]> into ]]\>
1023 |           if (i >= 2 &&
1024 |               ((s.charAt(i - 1) == '-' && s.charAt(i - 2) == '-') ||
1025 |                (s.charAt(i - 1) == ']' && s.charAt(i - 2) == ']'))) {
1026 |             sb.append("\\>");
1027 |           } else {
1028 |             sb.append(c);
1029 |           }
1030 |           break;
1031 |         case '<':
1032 |           // Break </script into <\/script
1033 |           final String END_SCRIPT = "/script";
1034 | 
1035 |           // Break <!-- into <\!--
1036 |           final String START_COMMENT = "!--";
1037 | 
1038 |           if (s.regionMatches(true, i + 1, END_SCRIPT, 0,
1039 |                               END_SCRIPT.length())) {
1040 |             sb.append("<\\");
1041 |           } else if (s.regionMatches(false, i + 1, START_COMMENT, 0,
1042 |                                      START_COMMENT.length())) {
1043 |             sb.append("<\\");
1044 |           } else {
1045 |             sb.append(c);
1046 |           }
1047 |           break;
1048 |         default:
1049 |           // If we're given an outputCharsetEncoder, then check if the
1050 |           //  character can be represented in this character set.
1051 |           if (outputCharsetEncoder != null) {
1052 |             if (outputCharsetEncoder.canEncode(c)) {
1053 |               sb.append(c);
1054 |             } else {
1055 |               // Unicode-escape the character.
1056 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1057 |             }
1058 |           } else {
1059 |             // No charsetEncoder provided - pass straight latin characters
1060 |             // through, and escape the rest.  Doing the explicit character
1061 |             // check is measurably faster than using the CharsetEncoder.
1062 |             if (c > 0x1f && c < 0x7f) {
1063 |               sb.append(c);
1064 |             } else {
1065 |               // Other characters can be misinterpreted by some js parsers,
1066 |               // or perhaps mangled by proxies along the way,
1067 |               // so we play it safe and unicode escape them.
1068 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1069 |             }
1070 |           }
1071 |       }
1072 |     }
1073 |     sb.append(quote);
1074 |     return sb.toString();
1075 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 164-193
Documentation:

Method code:
164 |   private Node tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(Node n) {
165 |     // Rewriting "(fn.bind(a,b))()" to "fn.call(a,b)" makes it inlinable
166 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.CALL);
167 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
168 |     Bind bind = getCodingConvention().describeFunctionBind(callTarget);
169 |     if (bind != null) {
170 |       // replace the call target
171 |       bind.target.detachFromParent();
172 |       n.replaceChild(callTarget, bind.target);
173 |       callTarget = bind.target;
174 | 
175 |       // push the parameters
176 |       addParameterAfter(bind.parameters, callTarget);
177 | 
178 |       // add the this value before the parameters if necessary
179 |       if (bind.thisValue != null && !NodeUtil.isUndefined(bind.thisValue)) {
180 |         // rewrite from "fn(a, b)" to "fn.call(thisValue, a, b)"
181 |         Node newCallTarget = new Node(Token.GETPROP,
182 |             callTarget.cloneTree(),
183 |             Node.newString("call").copyInformationFrom(callTarget));
184 |         n.replaceChild(callTarget, newCallTarget);
185 |         n.addChildAfter(bind.thisValue.cloneTree(), newCallTarget);
186 |         n.putBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL, false);
187 |       } else {
188 |         n.putBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL, true);
189 |       }
190 |       reportCodeChange();
191 |     }
192 |     return n;
193 |   }

===== M0069 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1632-1671
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1632 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1633 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1634 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1635 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1636 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1637 |       // {?} - right curly
1638 |       // {?=} - equals
1639 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1640 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1641 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1642 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1643 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1644 |       token = next();
1645 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1646 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1647 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1648 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1649 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1650 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1651 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1652 |       }
1653 | 
1654 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1655 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1656 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1657 |     } else {
1658 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1659 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1660 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1661 |           next();
1662 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1663 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1664 |           next();
1665 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1666 |         }
1667 |       }
1668 | 
1669 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1670 |     }
1671 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckAccidentalSemicolon.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckAccidentalSemicolon.java
Original range: 44-72
Documentation:

Method code:
44 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
45 |     Node child;
46 |     switch (n.getType()) {
47 |       case Token.IF:
48 |         child = n.getFirstChild().getNext();  // skip the condition child
49 |         break;
50 | 
51 |       case Token.WHILE:
52 |       case Token.FOR:
53 |         child = NodeUtil.getLoopCodeBlock(n);
54 |         break;
55 | 
56 |       default:
57 |         return;  // don't check other types
58 |     }
59 | 
60 |     // semicolons cause VOID children. Empty blocks are allowed because
61 |     // that's usually intentional, especially with loops.
62 |     for (; child != null; child = child.getNext()) {
63 |       if ((child.getType() == Token.BLOCK) && (!child.hasChildren())) {
64 |         // Only warn on empty blocks that replaced EMPTY nodes.  BLOCKs with no
65 |         // children are considered OK.
66 |         if (child.wasEmptyNode()) {
67 |           t.getCompiler().report(
68 |               t.makeError(n, level, SUSPICIOUS_SEMICOLON));
69 |         }
70 |       }
71 |     }
72 |   }

===== M0105 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.removeUnreferencedVars()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 779-845
Documentation:
/**
   * Removes any vars in the scope that were not referenced. Removes any
   * assignments to those variables as well.
   */
Method code:
779 |   private void removeUnreferencedVars() {
780 |     CodingConvention convention = codingConvention;
781 | 
782 |     for (Iterator<Var> it = maybeUnreferenced.iterator(); it.hasNext(); ) {
783 |       Var var = it.next();
784 | 
785 |       // Remove calls to inheritance-defining functions where the unreferenced
786 |       // class is the subclass.
787 |       for (Node exprCallNode : inheritsCalls.get(var)) {
788 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(exprCallNode.getParent(), exprCallNode);
789 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
790 |       }
791 | 
792 |       // Regardless of what happens to the original declaration,
793 |       // we need to remove all assigns, because they may contain references
794 |       // to other unreferenced variables.
795 |       removeAllAssigns(var);
796 | 
797 |       compiler.addToDebugLog("Unreferenced var: " + var.name);
798 |       Node nameNode = var.nameNode;
799 |       Node toRemove = nameNode.getParent();
800 |       Node parent = toRemove.getParent();
801 | 
802 |       Preconditions.checkState(
803 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR ||
804 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
805 |           toRemove.getType() == Token.LP &&
806 |           parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION,
807 |           "We should only declare vars and functions and function args");
808 | 
809 |       if (toRemove.getType() == Token.LP &&
810 |           parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
811 |         // Don't remove function arguments here. That's a special case
812 |         // that's taken care of in removeUnreferencedFunctionArgs.
813 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(toRemove)) {
814 |         if (!preserveFunctionExpressionNames) {
815 |           toRemove.getFirstChild().setString("");
816 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
817 |         }
818 |         // Don't remove bleeding functions.
819 |       } else if (parent != null &&
820 |           parent.getType() == Token.FOR &&
821 |           parent.getChildCount() < 4) {
822 |         // foreach iterations have 3 children. Leave them alone.
823 |       } else if (toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR &&
824 |           nameNode.hasChildren() &&
825 |           NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
826 |         // If this is a single var declaration, we can at least remove the
827 |         // declaration itself and just leave the value, e.g.,
828 |         // var a = foo(); => foo();
829 |         if (toRemove.getChildCount() == 1) {
830 |           parent.replaceChild(toRemove,
831 |               new Node(Token.EXPR_RESULT, nameNode.removeFirstChild()));
832 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
833 |         }
834 |       } else if (toRemove.getType() == Token.VAR &&
835 |           toRemove.getChildCount() > 1) {
836 |         // For var declarations with multiple names (i.e. var a, b, c),
837 |         // only remove the unreferenced name
838 |         toRemove.removeChild(nameNode);
839 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
840 |       } else if (parent != null) {
841 |         NodeUtil.removeChild(parent, toRemove);
842 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
843 |       }
844 |     }
845 |   }

   * Attempt to replace the condition of if or hook immediately that is a
   * reference to a name that is assigned immediately before.

494 |   private void tryOptimizeConditionalAfterAssign(Node n) {
495 |     Node next = n.getNext();
496 | 
497 |     // Look for patterns like the following and replace the if-condition with
498 |     // a constant value so it can later be folded:
499 |     //   var a = /a/;
500 |     //   if (a) {foo(a)}
501 |     // or
502 |     //   a = 0;
503 |     //   a ? foo(a) : c;
504 |     // or
505 |     //   a = 0;
506 |     //   a || foo(a);
507 |     // or
508 |     //   a = 0;
509 |     //   a && foo(a)
510 |     //
511 |     // TODO(johnlenz): This would be better handled by control-flow sensitive
512 |     // constant propagation. As the other case that I want to handle is:
513 |     //   i=0; for(;i<0;i++){}
514 |     // as right now nothing facilitates removing a loop like that.
515 |     // This is here simply to remove the cruft left behind goog.userAgent and
516 |     // similar cases.
517 | 
518 |     if (isSimpleAssignment(n) && isConditionalStatement(next)) {
519 |       Node lhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentName(n);
520 | 
521 |       Node condition = getConditionalStatementCondition(next);
522 |       if (NodeUtil.isName(lhsAssign) && NodeUtil.isName(condition)
523 |           && lhsAssign.getString().equals(condition.getString())) {
524 |         Node rhsAssign = getSimpleAssignmentValue(n);
525 |         TernaryValue value = NodeUtil.getImpureBooleanValue(rhsAssign);
526 |         if (value != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
527 |           int replacementConditionNodeType =
528 |             (value.toBoolean(true)) ? Token.TRUE : Token.FALSE;
529 |           condition.getParent().replaceChild(condition,

1298 |                  scriptNode != null;

1300 |               toSource(cb, i++, scriptNode);

===== M0151 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 727-870
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
727 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
728 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
729 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
730 |     // that we know to be safe
731 |     switch (n.getType()) {
732 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
733 |       case Token.AND:
734 |       case Token.BLOCK:
735 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
736 |       case Token.HOOK:
737 |       case Token.IF:
738 |       case Token.IN:
739 |       case Token.LP:
740 |       case Token.NUMBER:
741 |       case Token.OR:
742 |       case Token.THIS:
743 |       case Token.TRUE:
744 |       case Token.FALSE:
745 |       case Token.NULL:
746 |       case Token.STRING:
747 |       case Token.SWITCH:
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |       case Token.EMPTY:
750 |         break;
751 | 
752 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
753 |       case Token.THROW:
754 |         return true;
755 | 
756 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
757 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
758 |           return true;
759 |         }
760 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
761 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
762 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
763 |             return true;
764 |           }
765 |         }
766 |         return false;
767 | 
768 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
769 |       case Token.REGEXP:
770 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
771 |           return true;
772 |         }
773 |         break;
774 | 
775 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
776 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
777 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
778 |           return true;
779 |         }
780 |         break;
781 | 
782 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
783 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
784 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
785 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
786 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
787 | 
788 |       case Token.NEW:
789 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
790 |           return true;
791 |         }
792 | 
793 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
794 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
795 |           // side-effects
796 |           break;
797 |         }
798 |         return true;
799 | 
800 |       case Token.CALL:
801 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
802 |         // side effect property set.
803 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
804 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
805 |           // side-effects
806 |           break;
807 |         }
808 |         return true;
809 | 
810 |       default:
811 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
812 |           break;
813 |         }
814 | 
815 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
816 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
817 |           if (isName(assignTarget)) {
818 |             return true;
819 |           }
820 | 
821 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
822 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
823 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
824 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
825 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
826 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
827 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
828 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
829 |             return true;
830 |           }
831 | 
832 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
833 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
834 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
835 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
836 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
837 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
838 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
839 |               return false;
840 |             }
841 | 
842 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
843 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
844 |             // other objects.
845 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
846 |             // side-effect.
847 |             while (isGet(current)) {
848 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
849 |             }
850 | 
851 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
852 |           } else {
853 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
854 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
855 |             // preserve existing behavior.
856 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
857 |           }
858 |         }
859 | 
860 |         return true;
861 |     }
862 | 
863 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
864 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
865 |         return true;
866 |       }
867 |     }
868 | 
869 |     return false;
870 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal.traverseBranch(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeTraversal.java
Original range: 437-465
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses a branch.
   */
Method code:
437 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
438 |   private void traverseBranch(Node n, Node parent) {
439 |     int type = n.getType();
440 |     if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
441 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);
442 |     }
443 | 
444 |     curNode = n;
445 |     if (!callback.shouldTraverse(this, n, parent)) return;
446 |

454 |           // child could be replaced, in which case our child node

457 |           traverseBranch(child, n);

459 |         }
460 |         break;
461 |     }
462 | 
463 |     curNode = n;
464 |     callback.visit(this, n, parent);
465 |   }

/**
   * Checks whether a name can be referenced outside of the compiled code.
   * These names will be the root of dependency trees.
   *
   * @param scope The current variable scope
   * @param name The name
   * @return True if can be referenced outside
   */
Method code:
1456 |   private boolean isExternallyReferenceable(Scope scope, String name) {
1457 |     if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(name)) {
1458 |       return true;
1459 |     }

1461 |       return false;

1465 |         return true;
1466 |       }
1467 |     }
1468 |     return false;
1469 |   }

===== M0189 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.ReferenceCollection.isWellDefined()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 300-323
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines if the variable for this reference collection is
     * "well-defined." A variable is well-defined if we can prove at
     * compile-time that it's assigned a value before it's used.
     *
     * Notice that if this function returns false, this doesn't imply that the
     * variable is used before it's assigned. It just means that we don't
     * have enough information to make a definitive judgement.
     */
Method code:
300 |     protected boolean isWellDefined() {
301 |       int size = references.size();
302 |       if (size == 0) {
303 |         return false;
304 |       }
305 | 
306 |       // If this is a declaration that does not instantiate the variable,
307 |       // it's not well-defined.
308 |       Reference init = getInitializingReference();
309 |       if (init == null) {
310 |         return false;
311 |       }
312 | 
313 |       Preconditions.checkState(references.get(0).isDeclaration());
314 |       BasicBlock initBlock = init.getBasicBlock();
315 |       for (int i = 1; i < size; i++) {
316 |         if (!initBlock.provablyExecutesBefore(
317 |                 references.get(i).getBasicBlock())) {
318 |           return false;
319 |         }
320 |       }
321 | 
322 |       return true;
323 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFallThrough(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 786-800
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the destination node of n when we want to fallthough into the
   * subtree of n. We don't always create a CFG edge into n itself because of
   * DOs and FORs.
   */
Method code:
786 |   static Node computeFallThrough(Node n) {
787 |     switch (n.getType()) {
788 |       case Token.DO:
789 |         return computeFallThrough(n.getFirstChild());
790 |       case Token.FOR:
791 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
792 |           return n;
793 |         }
794 |         return computeFallThrough(n.getFirstChild());
795 |       case Token.LABEL:
796 |         return computeFallThrough(n.getLastChild());
797 |       default:
798 |         return n;
799 |     }
800 |   }

260 |   public void traverseRoots(List<Node> roots) {
261 |     if (roots.isEmpty()) {
262 |       return;
263 |     }

===== M0212 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckSideEffects.java
Original range: 47-118
Documentation:

Method code:
47 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
48 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
49 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
50 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
51 |     // so we'll allow it.
52 |     if (n.getType() == Token.EMPTY ||
53 |         n.getType() == Token.COMMA) {
54 |       return;
55 |     }
56 | 
57 |     if (parent == null)
58 |       return;
59 | 
60 |     int pt = parent.getType();
61 |     if (pt == Token.COMMA) {
62 |       Node gramps = parent.getParent();
63 |       if (gramps.getType() == Token.CALL &&
64 |           parent == gramps.getFirstChild()) {
65 |         // Semantically, a direct call to eval is different from an indirect
66 |         // call to an eval. See Ecma-262 S15.1.2.1. So it's ok for the first
67 |         // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
68 |         // an eval.
69 |         if (n == parent.getFirstChild() &&
70 |             parent.getChildCount() == 2 &&
71 |             n.getNext().getType() == Token.NAME &&
72 |             "eval".equals(n.getNext().getString())) {
73 |           return;
74 |         }
75 |       }
76 | 
77 |       if (n == parent.getLastChild()) {
78 |         for (Node an : parent.getAncestors()) {
79 |           int ancestorType = an.getType();
80 |           if (ancestorType == Token.COMMA)
81 |             continue;
82 |           if (ancestorType != Token.EXPR_RESULT &&
83 |               ancestorType != Token.BLOCK)
84 |             return;
85 |           else
86 |             break;
87 |         }
88 |       }
89 |     } else if (pt != Token.EXPR_RESULT && pt != Token.BLOCK) {
90 |       if (pt == Token.FOR && parent.getChildCount() == 4 &&
91 |           (n == parent.getFirstChild() ||
92 |            n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext())) {
93 |         // Fall through and look for warnings for the 1st and 3rd child
94 |         // of a for.
95 |       } else {
96 |         return;  // it might be ok to not have a side-effect
97 |       }
98 |     }
99 |     if (NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType()) ||
100 |         !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler())) {
101 |       if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
102 |         // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
103 |         // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
104 |         return;
105 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n)) {
106 |         // we already reported the problem when we visited the child.
107 |         return;
108 |       }
109 | 
110 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
111 |       if (n.getType() == Token.STRING) {
112 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
113 |       }
114 | 
115 |       t.getCompiler().report(
116 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
117 |     }

Original range: 577-609
Documentation:
/**
     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
     */
Method code:
577 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
578 |       Preconditions.checkState(
579 |           functionBody.getParent().getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
580 |       Node previous = null;
581 |       Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
582 |       // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
583 |       // are already in the right place.
584 |       while (current != null && NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
585 |         previous = current;
586 |         current = current.getNext();
587 |       }
588 | 
589 |       // Find any remaining declarations and move them.
590 |       Node insertAfter = previous;
591 |       while (current != null) {
592 |         // Save off the next node as the current node maybe removed.
593 |         Node next = current.getNext();
594 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(current)) {
595 |           // Remove the declaration from the body.
596 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(previous);
597 |           functionBody.removeChildAfter(previous);
598 | 
599 |           // Readd the function at the top of the function body (after any
600 |           // previous declarations).
601 |           insertAfter = addToFront(functionBody, current, insertAfter);
602 |           reportCodeChange("Move function declaration not at top of function");
603 |         } else {
604 |           // Update the previous only if the current node hasn't been moved.
605 |           previous = current;
606 |         }
607 |         current = next;
608 |       }
609 |     }

===== M0236 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 150-195
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
150 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
151 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
152 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
153 |       case Token.BLOCK:
154 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
155 |       case Token.TRY:
156 |       case Token.FINALLY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
184 |         } else {
185 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
186 |         }
187 |       case Token.SWITCH:
188 |       case Token.CASE:
189 |       case Token.CATCH:
190 |       case Token.WITH:
191 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
192 |       default:
193 |         return false;
194 |     }
195 |   }

933 |           String msg =
934 |               "Invalid delete operand. Only properties can be deleted.";;
935 |           errorReporter.error(
936 |               msg,
937 |               sourceName,
938 |               operand.getLineno(), "", 0);
939 |         } else  if (type == Token.INC || type == Token.DEC) {
940 |           if (!validAssignmentTarget(operand)) {
941 |             String msg = (type == Token.INC)
942 |                 ? "invalid increment target"
943 |                 : "invalid decrement target";
944 |             errorReporter.error(
945 |                 msg,
946 |                 sourceName,
947 |                 operand.getLineno(), "", 0);
948 |           }
949 |         }
950 | 
951 |         Node node = newNode(type, operand);
952 |         if (exprNode.isPostfix()) {
953 |           node.putBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP, true);
954 |         }
955 |         return node;
956 |       }
957 |     }

===== M0250 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PureFunctionIdentifier.FunctionAnalyzer.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PureFunctionIdentifier.java
Original range: 396-467
Documentation:

Method code:
396 |     @Override
397 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal traversal, Node node, Node parent) {
398 | 
399 |       if (inExterns) {
400 |         return;
401 |       }
402 | 
403 |       if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(node)
404 |           && node.getType() != Token.RETURN) {
405 |         return;
406 |       }
407 | 
408 |       if (NodeUtil.isCall(node) || NodeUtil.isNew(node)) {
409 |         allFunctionCalls.add(node);
410 |       }
411 | 
412 |       Node enclosingFunction = traversal.getEnclosingFunction();
413 |       if (enclosingFunction != null) {
414 |         FunctionInformation sideEffectInfo =
415 |             functionSideEffectMap.get(enclosingFunction);
416 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(sideEffectInfo);
417 | 
418 |         if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(node)) {
419 |           visitAssignmentOrUnaryOperator(
420 |               sideEffectInfo, traversal.getScope(),
421 |               node, node.getFirstChild(), node.getLastChild());
422 |         } else {
423 |           switch(node.getType()) {
424 |             case Token.CALL:
425 |             case Token.NEW:
426 |               visitCall(sideEffectInfo, node);
427 |               break;
428 |             case Token.DELPROP:
429 |             case Token.DEC:
430 |             case Token.INC:
431 |               visitAssignmentOrUnaryOperator(
432 |                   sideEffectInfo, traversal.getScope(),
433 |                   node, node.getFirstChild(), null);
434 |               break;
435 |             case Token.NAME:
436 |               // Variable definition are not side effects.
437 |               // Just check that the name appears in the context of a
438 |               // variable declaration.
439 |               Preconditions.checkArgument(
440 |                   NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(node));
441 |               Node value = node.getFirstChild();
442 |               // Assignment to local, if the value isn't a safe local value,
443 |               // new object creation or literal or known primitive result
444 |               // value, add it to the local blacklist.
445 |               if (value != null && !NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(value)) {
446 |                 Scope scope = traversal.getScope();
447 |                 Var var = scope.getVar(node.getString());
448 |                 sideEffectInfo.blacklistLocal(var);
449 |               }
450 |               break;
451 |             case Token.THROW:
452 |               visitThrow(sideEffectInfo);
453 |               break;
454 |             case Token.RETURN:
455 |               if (node.hasChildren()
456 |                   && !NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(node.getFirstChild())) {
457 |                 sideEffectInfo.setTaintsReturn();
458 |               }
459 |               break;
460 |             default:
461 |               throw new IllegalArgumentException(
462 |                   "Unhandled side effect node type " +
463 |                   Token.name(node.getType()));
464 |           }
465 |         }
466 |       }
467 |     }

===== M0287 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseAnonymousFunctions.Callback.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseAnonymousFunctions.java
Original range: 53-95
Documentation:

Method code:
53 |     @Override
54 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
55 |       if (n.getType() != Token.VAR) {
56 |         return;
57 |       }
58 | 
59 |       // It is only safe to collapse anonymous functions that appear
60 |       // at top-level blocks.  In other cases the difference between
61 |       // variable and function declarations can lead to problems or
62 |       // expose subtle bugs in browser implementation as function
63 |       // definitions are added to scopes before the start of execution.
64 | 
65 |       Node grandparent = parent.getParent();
66 |       if (!(parent.getType() == Token.SCRIPT ||
67 |             grandparent != null &&
68 |             grandparent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION &&
69 |             parent.getType() == Token.BLOCK)) {
70 |         return;
71 |       }
72 | 
73 |       // Need to store the next name in case the current name is removed from
74 |       // the linked list.
75 |       Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
76 |       Node name = n.getFirstChild();
77 |       Node value = name.getFirstChild();
78 |       if (value != null &&
79 |           value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION &&
80 |           !isRecursiveFunction(value)) {
81 |         Node fnName = value.getFirstChild();
82 |         fnName.setString(name.getString());
83 |         NodeUtil.copyNameAnnotations(name, fnName);
84 |         name.removeChild(value);
85 |         parent.replaceChild(n, value);
86 | 
87 |         // Renormalize the code.
88 |         if (!t.inGlobalScope() &&
89 |             NodeUtil.isHoistedFunctionDeclaration(value)) {
90 |           parent.addChildToFront(value.detachFromParent());
91 |         }
92 | 
93 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |       }
95 |     }

===== M0334 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.traverseNode(Node,Node,Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 190-294
Documentation:
/**
   * Traverses everything in the current scope and marks variables that
   * are referenced.
   *
   * During traversal, we identify subtrees that will only be
   * referenced if their enclosing variables are referenced. Instead of
   * traversing those subtrees, we create a continuation for them,
   * and traverse them lazily.
   */
Method code:
190 |   private void traverseNode(Node n, Node parent, Scope scope) {
191 |     int type = n.getType();
192 |     Var var = null;
193 |     switch (type) {
194 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
195 |         // If this function is a removable var, then create a continuation
196 |         // for it instead of traversing immediately.
197 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
198 |           var = scope.getVar(n.getFirstChild().getString());
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         if (var != null && isRemovableVar(var)) {
202 |           continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
203 |         } else {
204 |           traverseFunction(n, scope);
205 |         }
206 |         return;
207 | 
208 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
209 |         Assign maybeAssign = Assign.maybeCreateAssign(n);
210 |         if (maybeAssign != null) {
211 |           // Put this in the assign map. It might count as a reference,
212 |           // but we won't know that until we have an index of all assigns.
213 |           var = scope.getVar(maybeAssign.nameNode.getString());
214 |           if (var != null) {
215 |             assignsByVar.put(var, maybeAssign);
216 |             assignsByNode.put(maybeAssign.nameNode, maybeAssign);
217 | 
218 |             if (isRemovableVar(var) &&
219 |                 !maybeAssign.mayHaveSecondarySideEffects) {
220 |               // If the var is unreferenced and performing this assign has
221 |               // no secondary side effects, then we can create a continuation
222 |               // for it instead of traversing immediately.
223 |               continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
224 |               return;
225 |             }
226 |           }
227 |         }
228 |         break;
229 | 
230 |       case Token.CALL:
231 |         // Look for calls to inheritance-defining calls (such as goog.inherits).
232 |         SubclassRelationship subclassRelationship =
233 |             codingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall(n);
234 |         if (subclassRelationship != null) {
235 |           Var subclassVar = scope.getVar(subclassRelationship.subclassName);
236 |           // Don't try to track the inheritance calls for non-globals. It would
237 |           // be more correct to only not track when the subclass does not
238 |           // reference a constructor, but checking that it is a global is
239 |           // easier and mostly the same.
240 |           if (subclassVar != null && subclassVar.isGlobal()
241 |               && !referenced.contains(subclassVar)) {
242 |             // Save a reference to the EXPR node.
243 |             inheritsCalls.put(subclassVar, parent);
244 |             continuations.put(subclassVar, new Continuation(n, scope));
245 |             return;
246 |           }
247 |         }
248 |         break;
249 | 
250 |       case Token.NAME:
251 |         var = scope.getVar(n.getString());
252 |         if (parent.getType() == Token.VAR) {
253 |           Node value = n.getFirstChild();
254 |           if (value != null && var != null && isRemovableVar(var) &&
255 |               !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(value)) {
256 |             // If the var is unreferenced and creating its value has no side
257 |             // effects, then we can create a continuation for it instead
258 |             // of traversing immediately.
259 |             continuations.put(var, new Continuation(n, scope));
260 |             return;
261 |           }
262 |         } else {
263 | 
264 |           // If arguments is escaped, we just assume the worst and continue
265 |           // on all the parameters.
266 |           if ("arguments".equals(n.getString()) && scope.isLocal()) {
267 |             Node lp = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
268 |             for (Node a = lp.getFirstChild(); a != null; a = a.getNext()) {
269 |               markReferencedVar(scope.getVar(a.getString()));
270 |             }
271 |           }
272 | 
273 |           // All name references that aren't declarations or assigns
274 |           // are references to other vars.
275 |           if (var != null) {
276 |             // If that var hasn't already been marked referenced, then
277 |             // start tracking it.  If this is an assign, do nothing
278 |             // for now.
279 |             if (isRemovableVar(var)) {
280 |               if (!assignsByNode.containsKey(n)) {
281 |                 markReferencedVar(var);
282 |               }
283 |             } else {
284 |               markReferencedVar(var);
285 |             }
286 |           }
287 |         }
288 |         break;
289 |     }
290 | 
291 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
292 |       traverseNode(c, n, scope);
293 |     }
294 |   }

===== M0349 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 682-779
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
682 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
683 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
684 |     /*
685 |      * This is the case where:
686 |      *
687 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
688 |      * the script.
689 |      *
690 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
691 |      * the caller of the function.
692 |      *
693 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
694 |      * back to the caller of the function.
695 |      *
696 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
697 |      * asked to traverse.
698 |      *
699 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
700 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
701 |      */
702 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
703 |     if (parent == null || parent.getType() == Token.FUNCTION ||
704 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
705 |       return null;
706 |     }
707 | 
708 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
709 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
710 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
711 |       case Token.IF:
712 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
713 |       case Token.CASE:
714 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
715 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
716 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
717 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
718 |           if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.CASE) {
719 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
720 |           } else if (parent.getNext().getType() == Token.DEFAULT) {
721 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
722 |           } else {
723 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
724 |           }
725 |         } else {
726 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
727 |         }
728 |         break;
729 |       case Token.FOR:
730 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
731 |           return parent;
732 |         } else {
733 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
734 |         }
735 |       case Token.WHILE:
736 |       case Token.DO:
737 |         return parent;
738 |       case Token.TRY:
739 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
740 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
741 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
742 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
743 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
744 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
745 |           }
746 |         // CATCH block.
747 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
748 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
749 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
750 |           } else {
751 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
752 |           }
753 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
754 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
755 |           if (cfa != null) {
756 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
757 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
758 |             }
759 |           }
760 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
761 |         }
762 |     }
763 | 
764 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
765 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
766 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
767 | 
768 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
769 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
770 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
771 |     }
772 | 
773 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
774 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
775 |     } else {
776 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transfered up the AST.
777 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
778 |     }
779 |   }

345 |                 }

348 |                 return;
349 |               case Token.FUNCTION:

351 |                 if (gramps == null ||

355 |                 break;

391 |                     parent.getFirstChild() == n) {

418 |       }

97 |     // Handle all binary operators
98 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {

100 |           childCount == 2,
101 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
102 |           opstr, childCount);
103 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
104 |       addLeftExpr(first, p, context);
105 |       cc.addOp(opstr, true);
106 | 
107 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
108 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.

111 |       // Handle associativity.
112 |       // e.g. if the parse tree is a * (b * c),
113 |       // we can simply generate a * b * c.

116 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
117 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
118 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
119 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
120 |       } else {
121 |         addExpr(last, p + 1, rhsContext);
122 |       }
123 |       return;

471 |         break;
472 |       }
473 | 
474 |       case Token.GETELEM:
475 |         Preconditions.checkState(
476 |             childCount == 2,
477 |             "Bad GETELEM: expected 2 children but got %s", childCount);
478 |         addLeftExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
479 |         add("[");
480 |         add(first.getNext());
481 |         add("]");
482 |         break;
483 | 
484 |       case Token.WITH:
485 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
486 |         add("with(");
487 |         add(first);
488 |         add(")");
489 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
490 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
491 |         break;
492 | 
493 |       case Token.INC:
494 |       case Token.DEC: {
495 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
496 |         String o = type == Token.INC ? "++" : "--";
497 |         int postProp = n.getIntProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP);
498 |         // A non-zero post-prop value indicates a post inc/dec, default of zero
499 |         // is a pre-inc/dec.
500 |         if (postProp != 0) {
501 |           addLeftExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
502 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
503 |         } else {
504 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
505 |           add(first);
506 |         }
507 |         break;
508 |       }
509 | 
510 |       case Token.CALL:
511 |         // We have two special cases here:
512 |         // 1) If the left hand side of the call is a direct reference to eval,
513 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
514 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that
515 |         // indirectness must be preserved.
516 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,
517 |         // then the call must not a FREE_CALL annotation. If it does, then
518 |         // that means it was originally an call without an explicit this and
519 |         // that must be preserved.
520 |         if (isIndirectEval(first)
521 |             || n.getBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL) && NodeUtil.isGet(first)) {
522 |           add("(0,");
523 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.COMMA));
524 |           add(")");
525 |         } else {
526 |           addLeftExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
527 |         }
528 |         add("(");
529 |         addList(first.getNext());
530 |         add(")");
531 |         break;
532 | 
533 |       case Token.IF:
534 |         boolean hasElse = childCount == 3;
535 |         boolean ambiguousElseClause =
536 |             context == Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE && !hasElse;
537 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
538 |           cc.beginBlock();
539 |         }
540 | 
541 |         add("if(");
542 |         add(first);
543 |         add(")");
544 | 
545 |         if (hasElse) {
546 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
547 |               first.getNext(), Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE, false);
548 |           add("else");
549 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
550 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
551 |         } else {
552 |           addNonEmptyStatement(first.getNext(), Context.OTHER, false);
553 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
554 |         }
555 | 
556 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
557 |           cc.endBlock();
558 |         }
559 |         break;
560 | 
561 |       case Token.NULL:
562 |       case Token.THIS:
563 |       case Token.FALSE:
564 |       case Token.TRUE:
565 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
566 |         add(Node.tokenToName(type));
567 |         break;
568 | 
569 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
570 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
571 |         add("continue");
572 |         if (childCount == 1) {
573 |           if (first.getType() != Token.LABEL_NAME) {
574 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
575 |           }
576 |           add(" ");
577 |           add(first);
578 |         }
579 |         cc.endStatement();
580 |         break;
581 | 
582 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
583 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
584 |         add("debugger");
585 |         cc.endStatement();
586 |         break;
587 | 
588 |       case Token.BREAK:
589 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
590 |         add("break");
591 |         if (childCount == 1) {
592 |           if (first.getType() != Token.LABEL_NAME) {
593 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
594 |           }
595 |           add(" ");
596 |           add(first);
597 |         }
598 |         cc.endStatement();
599 |         break;
600 | 
601 |       case Token.EXPR_VOID:
602 |         throw new Error("Unexpected EXPR_VOID. Should be EXPR_RESULT.");
603 | 
604 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
605 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
606 |         add(first, Context.START_OF_EXPR);
607 |         cc.endStatement();
608 |         break;
609 | 
610 |       case Token.NEW:
611 |         add("new ");
612 |         int precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
613 | 
614 |         // If the first child contains a CALL, then claim higher precedence
615 |         // to force parentheses. Otherwise, when parsed, NEW will bind to the
616 |         // first viable parentheses (don't traverse into functions).
617 |         if (NodeUtil.containsType(first, Token.CALL, new MatchNotFunction())) {
618 |           precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType()) + 1;
619 |         }
620 |         addExpr(first, precedence);
621 | 
622 |         // '()' is optional when no arguments are present
623 |         Node next = first.getNext();
624 |         if (next != null) {
625 |           add("(");
626 |           addList(next);
627 |           add(")");
628 |         }
629 |         break;
630 | 
631 |       case Token.STRING:
632 |         if (childCount !=
633 |             ((n.getParent() != null &&
634 |               n.getParent().getType() == Token.OBJECTLIT) ? 1 : 0)) {
635 |           throw new IllegalStateException(
636 |               "Unexpected String children: " + n.getParent().toStringTree());
637 |         }
638 |         addJsString(n.getString());
639 |         break;
640 | 
641 |       case Token.DELPROP:
642 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
643 |         add("delete ");
644 |         add(first);
645 |         break;
646 | 
647 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
648 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
649 |         if (needsParens) {
650 |           add("(");
651 |         }
652 |         add("{");
653 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
654 |           if (c != first) {
655 |             cc.listSeparator();
656 |           }
657 | 
658 |           if (c.getType() == Token.GET || c.getType() == Token.SET) {
659 |             add(c);
660 |           } else {
661 |             Preconditions.checkState(c.getType() == Token.STRING);
662 |             String key = c.getString();
663 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they
664 |             // are not JavaScript keywords
665 |             if (!c.isQuotedString() &&
666 |                 !TokenStream.isKeyword(key) &&
667 |                 TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key) &&
668 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that
669 |                 // were unicode escaped.
670 |                 NodeUtil.isLatin(key)) {
671 |               add(key);
672 |             } else {
673 |               // Determine if the string is a simple number.
674 |               double d = getSimpleNumber(key);
675 |               if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
676 |                 cc.addNumber(d);
677 |               } else {
678 |                 addExpr(c, 1);
679 |               }
680 |             }
681 |             add(":");
682 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1);
683 |           }
684 |         }
685 |         add("}");
686 |         if (needsParens) {
687 |           add(")");
688 |         }
689 |         break;
690 |       }
691 | 
692 |       case Token.SWITCH:
693 |         add("switch(");
694 |         add(first);
695 |         add(")");
696 |         cc.beginBlock();
697 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
698 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
699 |         break;
700 | 
701 |       case Token.CASE:
702 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
703 |         add("case ");
704 |         add(first);
705 |         addCaseBody(last);
706 |         break;
707 | 
708 |       case Token.DEFAULT:
709 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
710 |         add("default");
711 |         addCaseBody(first);
712 |         break;
713 | 
714 |       case Token.LABEL:
715 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
716 |         if (first.getType() != Token.LABEL_NAME) {
717 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
718 |         }
719 |         add(first);
720 |         add(":");
721 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
722 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
723 |         break;
724 | 
725 |       // This node is auto generated in anonymous functions and should just get
726 |       // ignored for our purposes.
727 |       case Token.SETNAME:
728 |         break;
729 | 
730 |       default:
731 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
732 |     }
733 | 
734 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
735 |   }

806 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
807 |       if (!(NodeUtil.isName(n) ||
808 |             NodeUtil.isGet(n) && !NodeUtil.isGetProp(parent))) {
809 |         // This is not a simple or qualified name.
810 |         return;
811 |       }
812 | 
813 |       NameInformation nameInfo = createNameInformation(t, n, parent);
814 |       if (nameInfo == null) {
815 |         // The name is not a global name
816 |         return;
817 |       }
818 | 
819 |       if (nameInfo.onlyAffectsClassDef) {
820 |         if (nameInfo.superclass != null) {
821 |           recordReference(
822 |               nameInfo.name, nameInfo.superclass, RefType.INHERITANCE);
823 |         }
824 | 
825 |         // Make sure that we record a reference to the function that does
826 |         // the inheritance, so that the inherits() function itself does
827 |         // not get stripped.
828 |         String nodeName = n.getQualifiedName();
829 |         if (nodeName != null) {
830 |           recordReference(
831 |               nameInfo.name, nodeName, RefType.REGULAR);
832 |         }
833 | 
834 |         return;
835 |       }
836 | 
837 |       if (parent.getType() == Token.INSTANCEOF &&
838 |           parent.getLastChild() == n &&
839 |           // Don't cover GETELEMs with a global root node.
840 |           n.isQualifiedName()) {
841 |         JsName checkedClass = getName(nameInfo.name, true);
842 |         refNodes.add(
843 |             new InstanceOfCheckNode(
844 |                 checkedClass, n, parent, parent.getParent()));
845 |         checkedClass.hasInstanceOfReference = true;
846 |         return;
847 |       }
848 | 
849 |       // Determine which name might be potentially referring to this one by
850 |       // looking up the nearest enclosing dependency scope. It's unnecessary to
851 |       // determine all enclosing dependency scopes because this callback should
852 |       // create a chain of references between them.
853 |       NameInformation referring = getDependencyScope(n);
854 |       String referringName = "";
855 |       if (referring != null) {
856 |         referringName = referring.isPrototype
857 |                       ? referring.prototypeClass
858 |                       : referring.name;
859 |       }
860 | 
861 |       String name = nameInfo.name;
862 | 
863 |       // A value whose result is the return value of a function call
864 |       // can be an alias to global object.
865 |       // Here we add a alias to the general "global" object
866 |       // to act as a placeholder for the actual (unnamed) value.
867 |       if (maybeHiddenAlias(name, n)) {
868 |         recordAlias(name, WINDOW);
869 |       }
870 | 
871 |       // An externally referenceable name must always be defined, so we add a
872 |       // reference to it from the global scope (a.k.a. window).
873 |       if (nameInfo.isExternallyReferenceable) {
874 |         recordReference(WINDOW, name, RefType.REGULAR);
875 |         maybeRecordAlias(name, parent, referring, referringName);
876 |         return;
877 |       }
878 | 
879 |       // An assignment implies a reference from the enclosing dependency scope.
880 |       // For example, foo references bar in: function foo() {bar=5}.
881 |       if (NodeUtil.isVarOrSimpleAssignLhs(n, parent)) {
882 |         if (referring != null) {
883 |           recordReference(referringName, name, RefType.REGULAR);
884 |         }
885 |         return;
886 |       }
887 | 
888 |       if (nodesToKeep.contains(n)) {
889 |         NameInformation functionScope = getEnclosingFunctionDependencyScope(t);
890 |         if (functionScope != null) {
891 |           recordReference(functionScope.name, name, RefType.REGULAR);
892 |         } else {
893 |           recordReference(WINDOW, name, RefType.REGULAR);
894 |         }
895 |       } else if (referring != null) {
896 |         if (!maybeRecordAlias(name, parent, referring, referringName)) {
897 |           RefType depType = referring.onlyAffectsClassDef ?
898 |               RefType.INHERITANCE : RefType.REGULAR;
899 |           recordReference(referringName, name, depType);
900 |         }
901 |       } else {
902 |         // No named dependency scope found.  Unfortunately that might
903 |         // mean that the expression is a child of an function expression
904 |         // or assignment with a complex lhs.  In those cases,
905 |         // protect this node by creating a reference to WINDOW.
906 |         for (Node ancestor : n.getAncestors()) {
907 |           if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(ancestor) ||
908 |               NodeUtil.isFunction(ancestor)) {
909 |             recordReference(WINDOW, name, RefType.REGULAR);
910 |             break;
911 |           }
912 |         }
913 |       }
914 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MethodCompilerPass.GatherSignatures.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)

Method code:
180 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
181 |       switch (n.getType()) {
182 |         case Token.GETPROP:
183 |         case Token.GETELEM:
184 |           Node dest = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
185 | 
186 |           if (dest.getType() == Token.STRING) {
187 |             if (dest.getString().equals("prototype")) {
188 |               processPrototypeParent(t, parent);
189 |             } else {
190 |               // Static methods of the form Foo.bar = function() {} or
191 |               // Static methods of the form Foo.bar = baz (where baz is a
192 |               // function name). Parse tree looks like:
193 |               // assign                 <- parent
194 |               //      getprop           <- n
195 |               //          name Foo
196 |               //          string bar
197 |               //      function or name  <- n.getNext()
198 |               if (parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
199 |                   parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
200 |                 addPossibleSignature(dest.getString(), n.getNext(), t);
201 |               }
202 |             }
203 |           }
204 |           break;
205 | 
206 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
207 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
208 |             switch(key.getType()) {
209 |               case Token.STRING:
210 |                 addPossibleSignature(key.getString(), key.getFirstChild(), t);
211 |                 break;
212 |               case Token.SET:
213 |               case Token.GET:
214 |                 nonMethodProperties.add(key.getString());
215 |                 break;
216 |               default:
217 |                 throw new IllegalStateException(
218 |                     "unexpect OBJECTLIT key: " + key);
219 |             }
220 |           }
221 |           break;
222 |       }
223 |     }

1157 |   private void outputManifestOrBundle(List<String> outputFiles,
1158 |       boolean isManifest) throws IOException {
1159 |     if (outputFiles.isEmpty()) {
1160 |       return;
1161 |     }

1169 |       if (shouldGenerateOutputPerModule(output)) {

1172 |         for (JSModule module : modules) {

1174 |               expandCommandLinePath(output, module));
1175 |           if (isManifest) {
1176 |             printManifestTo(module.getInputs(), out);
1177 |           } else {
1178 |             printBundleTo(module.getInputs(), out);
1179 |           }
1180 |           out.close();
1181 |         }
1182 |       } else {
1183 |         // Generate a single file manifest or bundle.
1184 |         Writer out = fileNameToOutputWriter(
1185 |             expandCommandLinePath(output, null));
1186 |         if (graph == null) {
1187 |           if (isManifest) {
1188 |             printManifestTo(compiler.getInputsInOrder(), out);
1189 |           } else {
1190 |             printBundleTo(compiler.getInputsInOrder(), out);
1191 |           }
1192 |         } else {
1193 |           printModuleGraphManifestOrBundleTo(graph, out, isManifest);
1194 |         }
1195 |         out.close();
1196 |       }
1197 |     }
1198 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeReplaceKnownMethods.tryFoldArrayJoin(Node)
