Original range: 363-468
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to fold an array join: ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('') -> 'abc';
   */
Method code:
363 |   private Node tryFoldArrayJoin(Node n) {
364 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
365 | 
366 |     if (callTarget == null || !NodeUtil.isGetProp(callTarget)) {
367 |       return n;
368 |     }
369 | 
370 |     Node right = callTarget.getNext();
371 |     if (right != null && !NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(right)) {
372 |       return n;
373 |     }
374 | 
375 |     Node arrayNode = callTarget.getFirstChild();
376 |     Node functionName = arrayNode.getNext();
377 | 
378 |     if ((arrayNode.getType() != Token.ARRAYLIT) ||
379 |         !functionName.getString().equals("join")) {
380 |       return n;
381 |     }
382 | 
383 |     String joinString = (right == null) ? "," : NodeUtil.getStringValue(right);
384 |     List<Node> arrayFoldedChildren = Lists.newLinkedList();
385 |     StringBuilder sb = null;
386 |     int foldedSize = 0;
387 |     Node prev = null;
388 |     Node elem = arrayNode.getFirstChild();
389 |     // Merges adjacent String nodes.
390 |     while (elem != null) {
391 |       if (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(elem) || elem.getType() == Token.EMPTY) {
392 |         if (sb == null) {
393 |           sb = new StringBuilder();
394 |         } else {
395 |           sb.append(joinString);
396 |         }
397 |         sb.append(NodeUtil.getArrayElementStringValue(elem));
398 |       } else {
399 |         if (sb != null) {
400 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
401 |           // + 2 for the quotes.
402 |           foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
403 |           arrayFoldedChildren.add(
404 |               Node.newString(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
405 |           sb = null;
406 |         }
407 |         foldedSize += InlineCostEstimator.getCost(elem);
408 |         arrayFoldedChildren.add(elem);
409 |       }
410 |       prev = elem;
411 |       elem = elem.getNext();
412 |     }
413 | 
414 |     if (sb != null) {
415 |       Preconditions.checkNotNull(prev);
416 |       // + 2 for the quotes.
417 |       foldedSize += sb.length() + 2;
418 |       arrayFoldedChildren.add(
419 |           Node.newString(sb.toString()).copyInformationFrom(prev));
420 |     }
421 |     // one for each comma.
422 |     foldedSize += arrayFoldedChildren.size() - 1;
423 | 
424 |     int originalSize = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(n);
425 |     switch (arrayFoldedChildren.size()) {
426 |       case 0:
427 |         Node emptyStringNode = Node.newString("");
428 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, emptyStringNode);
429 |         reportCodeChange();
430 |         return emptyStringNode;
431 |       case 1:
432 |         Node foldedStringNode = arrayFoldedChildren.remove(0);
433 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
434 |           return n;
435 |         }
436 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
437 |         if (foldedStringNode.getType() != Token.STRING) {
438 |           // If the Node is not a string literal, ensure that
439 |           // it is coerced to a string.
440 |           Node replacement = new Node(Token.ADD,
441 |               Node.newString("").copyInformationFrom(n),
442 |               foldedStringNode);
443 |           foldedStringNode = replacement;
444 |         }
445 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, foldedStringNode);
446 |         reportCodeChange();
447 |         return foldedStringNode;
448 |       default:
449 |         // No folding could actually be performed.
450 |         if (arrayFoldedChildren.size() == arrayNode.getChildCount()) {
451 |           return n;
452 |         }
453 |         int kJoinOverhead = "[].join()".length();
454 |         foldedSize += kJoinOverhead;
455 |         foldedSize += (right != null) ? InlineCostEstimator.getCost(right) : 0;
456 |         if (foldedSize > originalSize) {
457 |           return n;
458 |         }
459 |         arrayNode.detachChildren();
460 |         for (Node node : arrayFoldedChildren) {
461 |           arrayNode.addChildToBack(node);
462 |         }
463 |         reportCodeChange();
464 |         break;
465 |     }
466 | 
467 |     return n;
468 |   }

/**
   * Propagate side effect information by building a graph based on
   * call site information stored in FunctionInformation and the
   * DefinitionProvider and then running GraphReachability to
   * determine the set of functions that have side effects.
   */
Method code:
252 |   private void propagateSideEffects() {
253 |     // Nodes are function declarations; Edges are function call sites.
254 |     DiGraph<FunctionInformation, Node> sideEffectGraph =
255 |         LinkedDirectedGraph.createWithoutAnnotations();
256 | 
257 |     // create graph nodes
258 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
259 |       sideEffectGraph.createNode(functionInfo);
260 |     }
261 | 
262 |     // add connections to called functions and side effect root.
263 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
264 |       if (!functionInfo.mayHaveSideEffects()) {
265 |         continue;
266 |       }
267 | 
268 |       for (Node callSite : functionInfo.getCallsInFunctionBody()) {
269 |         Node callee = callSite.getFirstChild();
270 |         Collection<Definition> defs =
271 |             getCallableDefinitions(definitionProvider, callee);
272 |         if (defs == null) {
273 |           // Definition set is not complete or eligible.  Possible
274 |           // causes include:
275 |           //  * "callee" is not of type NAME or GETPROP.
276 |           //  * One or more definitions are not functions.
277 |           //  * One or more definitions are complex.
278 |           //    (e.i. return value of a call that returns a function).
279 |           functionInfo.setTaintsUnknown();
280 |           break;
281 |         }
282 | 
283 |         for (Definition def : defs) {
284 |           Node defValue = def.getRValue();
285 |           FunctionInformation dep = functionSideEffectMap.get(defValue);
286 |           Preconditions.checkNotNull(dep);
287 |           sideEffectGraph.connect(dep, callSite, functionInfo);
288 |         }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 | 
292 |     // Propagate side effect information to a fixed point.
293 |     FixedPointGraphTraversal.newTraversal(new SideEffectPropagationCallback())
294 |         .computeFixedPoint(sideEffectGraph);
295 | 
296 |     // Mark remaining functions "pure".
297 |     for (FunctionInformation functionInfo : functionSideEffectMap.values()) {
298 |       if (functionInfo.mayBePure()) {
299 |         functionInfo.setIsPure();
300 |       }
301 |     }

===== M0461 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CollapseProperties.inlineAliases(GlobalNamespace)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CollapseProperties.java
Original range: 160-196
Documentation:
/**
   * For each qualified name N in the global scope, we check if:
   * (a) No ancestor of N is ever aliased or assigned an unknown value type.
   *     (If N = "a.b.c", "a" and "a.b" are never aliased).
   * (b) N has exactly one write, and it lives in the global scope.
   * (c) N is aliased in a local scope.
   *
   * If (a) is true, then GlobalNamespace must know all the writes to N.
   * If (a) and (b) are true, then N cannot change during the execution of
   *    a local scope.
   * If (a) and (b) and (c) are true, then the alias can be inlined if the
   *    alias obeys the usual rules for how we decide whether a variable is
   *    inlineable.
   * @see InlineVariables
   */
Method code:
160 |   private void inlineAliases(GlobalNamespace namespace) {
161 |     // Invariant: All the names in the worklist meet condition (a).
162 |     Deque<Name> workList = new ArrayDeque<Name>(namespace.getNameForest());
163 |     while (!workList.isEmpty()) {
164 |       Name name = workList.pop();
165 | 
166 |       // Don't attempt to inline a getter or setter property as a variable.
167 |       if (name.type == Name.Type.GET || name.type == Name.Type.SET) {
168 |         continue;
169 |       }
170 | 
171 |       if (name.globalSets == 1 && name.localSets == 0 &&
172 |           name.aliasingGets > 0) {
173 |         // {@code name} meets condition (b). Find all of its local aliases
174 |         // and try to inline them.
175 |         List<Ref> refs = Lists.newArrayList(name.getRefs());
176 |         for (Ref ref : refs) {
177 |           if (ref.type == Type.ALIASING_GET && ref.scope.isLocal()) {
178 |             // {@code name} meets condition (c). Try to inline it.
179 |             if (inlineAliasIfPossible(ref, namespace)) {
180 |               name.removeRef(ref);
181 |             }
182 |           }
183 |         }
184 |       }
185 | 
186 |       // Check if {@code name} has any aliases left after the
187 |       // local-alias-inlining above.
188 |       if ((name.type == Name.Type.OBJECTLIT ||
189 |            name.type == Name.Type.FUNCTION) &&
190 |           name.aliasingGets == 0 && name.props != null) {
191 |         // All of {@code name}'s children meet condition (a), so they can be
192 |         // added to the worklist.
193 |         workList.addAll(name.props);
194 |       }
195 |     }
196 |   }

===== M0504 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 117-170
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
117 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
118 |     switch (n.getType()) {
119 |       case Token.VAR:
120 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
121 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
122 |              child != null;) {
123 |           Node next = child.getNext();
124 |           declareVar(child);
125 |           child = next;
126 |         }
127 |         return;
128 | 
129 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
130 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
131 |           return;
132 |         }
133 | 
134 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
135 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
136 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
137 |           return;
138 |         }
139 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
140 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
141 | 
142 |       case Token.CATCH:
143 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
144 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME);
145 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
146 |         // is the code block
147 | 
148 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
149 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
150 | 
151 |         declareVar(var);
152 |         scanVars(block, n);
153 |         return;  // only one child to scan
154 | 
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |         sourceName = n.getSourceFileName();
157 |         break;
158 |     }
159 | 
160 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
161 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
162 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
163 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
164 |            child != null;) {
165 |         Node next = child.getNext();
166 |         scanVars(child, n);
167 |         child = next;
168 |       }
169 |     }
170 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.functionCallHasSideEffects(Node,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 930-987
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if calls to this function have side effects.
   *
   * @param callNode The call node to inspected.
   * @param compiler A compiler object to provide program state changing
   *     context information. Can be null.
   */
Method code:
930 |   static boolean functionCallHasSideEffects(
931 |       Node callNode, @Nullable AbstractCompiler compiler) {
932 |     if (callNode.getType() != Token.CALL) {
933 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
934 |           "Expected CALL node, got " + Token.name(callNode.getType()));
935 |     }
936 | 
937 |     if (callNode.isNoSideEffectsCall()) {
938 |       return false;
939 |     }
940 | 
941 |     Node nameNode = callNode.getFirstChild();
942 | 
943 |     // Built-in functions with no side effects.
944 |     if (nameNode.getType() == Token.NAME) {
945 |       String name = nameNode.getString();
946 |       if (BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(name)) {
947 |         return false;
948 |       }
949 |     } else if (nameNode.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
950 |       if (callNode.hasOneChild()
951 |           && OBJECT_METHODS_WITHOUT_SIDEEFFECTS.contains(
952 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
953 |         return false;
954 |       }
955 | 
956 |       if (callNode.isOnlyModifiesThisCall()
957 |           && evaluatesToLocalValue(nameNode.getFirstChild())) {
958 |         return false;
959 |       }
960 | 
961 |       // Math.floor has no sideeffects.
962 |       // TODO(nicksantos): This is a terrible terrible hack, until
963 |       // I create a definitionprovider that understands namespacing.
964 |       if (nameNode.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.NAME) {
965 |         if ("Math.floor".equals(nameNode.getQualifiedName())) {
966 |           return false;
967 |         }
968 |       }
969 | 
970 |       if (compiler != null && !compiler.hasRegExpGlobalReferences()) {
971 |         if (nameNode.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.REGEXP
972 |             && REGEXP_METHODS.contains(nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
973 |           return false;
974 |         } else if (nameNode.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.STRING
975 |             && STRING_REGEXP_METHODS.contains(
976 |                 nameNode.getLastChild().getString())) {
977 |           Node param = nameNode.getNext();
978 |           if (param != null &&
979 |               (param.getType() == Token.STRING
980 |                   || param.getType() == Token.REGEXP))
981 |           return false;
982 |         }
983 |       }
984 |     }
985 | 
986 |     return true;
987 |   }

===== M0510 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

Documentation:
/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
820 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
821 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
822 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
823 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
824 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunction(handler)) {
825 |           return;
826 |         }

828 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
829 | 
830 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
831 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
832 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
833 |           } else {
834 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
835 |           }
836 |         } else { // Has a catch.
837 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
838 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
839 |             return;
840 |           } else {
841 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
842 |           }
843 |         }
844 |         lastJump = handler;
845 |       }
846 |     }
847 |   }

/**
   * Tells the type system that {@code owner} may have a property named
   * {@code propertyName}. This allows the registry to keep track of what
   * types a property is defined upon.
   *
   * This is NOT the same as saying that {@code owner} must have a property
   * named type. ObjectType#hasProperty attempts to minimize false positives
   * ("if we're not sure, then don't type check this property"). The type
   * registry, on the other hand, should attempt to minimize false negatives
   * ("if this property is assigned anywhere in the program, it must
   * show up in the type registry").
   */
Method code:

611 |       typesIndexedByProperty.put(propertyName, typeSet);
612 |     }
613 | 
614 |     typeSet.addAlternate(type);
615 |     addReferenceTypeIndexedByProperty(propertyName, type);

618 |     greatestSubtypeByProperty.remove(propertyName);

608 |         // Old Rhino tagged the empty name node with the line number of the
609 |         // declaration.
610 |         newName.setLineno(functionNode.getLineno());
611 |         // TODO(bowdidge) Mark line number of paren correctly.
612 |         // Same problem as below - the left paren might not be on the
613 |         // same line as the function keyword.
614 |         int lpColumn = functionNode.getAbsolutePosition() +
615 |             functionNode.getLp();
616 |         newName.setCharno(position2charno(lpColumn));
617 |       }
618 | 
619 |       node.addChildToBack(newName);
620 |       Node lp = newNode(Token.LP);
621 |       // The left paren's complicated because it's not represented by an
622 |       // AstNode, so there's nothing that has the actual line number that it
623 |       // appeared on.  We know the paren has to appear on the same line as the
624 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
625 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.
626 |       // TODO(bowdidge): Mark line number of paren correctly.
627 |       Name fnName = functionNode.getFunctionName();
628 |       if (fnName != null) {
629 |         lp.setLineno(fnName.getLineno());
630 |       } else {
631 |         lp.setLineno(functionNode.getLineno());
632 |       }
633 |       int lparenCharno = functionNode.getLp() +
634 |           functionNode.getAbsolutePosition();
635 | 
636 |       lp.setCharno(position2charno(lparenCharno));
637 |       for (AstNode param : functionNode.getParams()) {
638 |         lp.addChildToBack(transform(param));
639 |       }
640 |       node.addChildToBack(lp);
641 | 
642 |       Node bodyNode = transform(functionNode.getBody());
643 |       parseDirectives(bodyNode);
644 |       node.addChildToBack(bodyNode);
645 |      return node;
646 |     }

52 |   @Override
53 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
54 |     GraphNode<Node, Branch> gNode = t.getControlFlowGraph().getNode(n);
55 |     if (gNode != null && gNode.getAnnotation() != GraphReachability.REACHABLE) {
56 | 
57 |       // Only report error when there are some line number informations.

63 |           n.getType() != Token.EMPTY && n.getType() != Token.BREAK) {

65 |         // From now on, we are going to assume the user fixed the error and not
66 |         // give more warning related to code section reachable from this node.
67 |         new GraphReachability<Node, ControlFlowGraph.Branch>(
68 |             t.getControlFlowGraph()).recompute(n);
69 |

71 |         return false;

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:

1274 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {
1275 |       return -1;
1276 |     } else if ((charno & ~COLUMN_MASK) != 0) {
1277 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;
1278 |     } else {

===== M0613 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/FunctionType.java
Original range: 832-874
Documentation:
/**
   * A function is a subtype of another if their call methods are related via
   * subtyping and {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that} with regard to
   * the prototype chain.
   */
Method code:
832 |   @Override
833 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
834 |     if (JSType.isSubtype(this, that)) {
835 |       return true;
836 |     }
837 | 
838 |     if (that.isFunctionType()) {
839 |       if (((FunctionType) that).isInterface()) {
840 |         // Any function can be assigned to an interface function.
841 |         return true;
842 |       }
843 |       if (this.isInterface()) {
844 |         // An interface function cannot be assigned to anything.
845 |         return false;
846 |       }
847 |       // If functionA is a subtype of functionB, then their "this" types
848 |       // should be contravariant. However, this causes problems because
849 |       // of the way we enforce overrides. Because function(this:SubFoo)
850 |       // is not a subtype of function(this:Foo), our override check treats
851 |       // this as an error. It also screws up out standard method
852 |       // for aliasing constructors. Let's punt on all this for now.
853 |       // TODO(nicksantos): fix this.
854 |       FunctionType other = (FunctionType) that;
855 |       boolean treatThisTypesAsCovariant =
856 |         // If either one of these is a ctor, skip 'this' checking.
857 |         this.isConstructor() || other.isConstructor() ||
858 | 
859 |         // An interface 'this'-type is non-restrictive.
860 |         // In practical terms, if C implements I, and I has a method m,
861 |         // then any m doesn't necessarily have to C#m's 'this'
862 |         // type doesn't need to match I.
863 |         (other.typeOfThis.getConstructor() != null &&
864 |              other.typeOfThis.getConstructor().isInterface()) ||
865 | 
866 |         // If one of the 'this' types is covariant of the other,
867 |         // then we'll treat them as covariant (see comment above).
868 |         other.typeOfThis.isSubtype(this.typeOfThis) ||
869 |         this.typeOfThis.isSubtype(other.typeOfThis);
870 |       return treatThisTypesAsCovariant && this.call.isSubtype(other.call);
871 |     }
872 | 
873 |     return getNativeType(JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_PROTOTYPE).isSubtype(that);
874 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ShadowVariables.DoShadowVariables.enterScope(NodeTraversal)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ShadowVariables.java
Original range: 175-226

Method code:
175 |     @Override
176 |     public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
177 |       Scope s = t.getScope();
178 |       if (!s.isLocal()) {
179 |         return;
180 |       }
181 | 
182 |       // Since we don't shadow global, there is nothing to be done in the
183 |       // first immediate local scope as well.
184 |       if (s.getParent().isGlobal()) {
185 |         return;
186 |       }
187 | 
188 |       for (Iterator<Var> vars = s.getVars(); vars.hasNext();) {
189 |         Var var = vars.next();
190 | 
191 |         // Don't shadow variables that is bleed-out to fix an IE bug.
192 |         if (var.isBleedingFunction()) {
193 |           continue;
194 |         }
195 | 
196 |         // Don't shadow an exported local.
197 |         if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name, s.isLocal())) {
198 |           continue;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         // Try to look for the best shadow for the current candidate.
202 |         Assignment bestShadow = findBestShadow(s, var);
203 |         if (bestShadow == null) {
204 |           continue;
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         // The name assignment being shadowed.
208 |         Assignment localAssignment = assignments.get(var.getName());
209 | 
210 |         // Only shadow if this increases the number of occurrences of the
211 |         // shadowed variable.
212 |         if (bestShadow.count < localAssignment.count) {
213 |           continue; // Hope the next local variable would have a smaller count.
214 |         }
215 | 
216 |         doShadow(localAssignment, bestShadow, var);
217 | 
218 |         if (oldPseudoNameMap != null) {
219 |           String targetPseudoName =
220 |             oldPseudoNameMap.get(s.getVar(bestShadow.oldName).nameNode);
221 |           for (Node use : varToNameUsage.get(var)) {
222 |             deltaPseudoNameMap.put(use, targetPseudoName);
223 |           }
224 |         }
225 |       }
226 |     }

===== M0630 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 758-804
Documentation:

Method code:
758 |     public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
759 |       if (parent == null) {
760 |         return true;
761 |       }
762 | 
763 |       // Gather the list of nodes that either have side effects, are
764 |       // arguments to function calls with side effects or are used in
765 |       // control structure predicates.  These names are always
766 |       // referenced when the enclosing function is called.
767 |       if (n.getType() == Token.FOR) {
768 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
769 |           Node decl = n.getFirstChild();
770 |           Node pred = decl.getNext();
771 |           Node step = pred.getNext();
772 |           addSimplifiedExpression(decl, n);
773 |           addSimplifiedExpression(pred, n);
774 |           addSimplifiedExpression(step, n);
775 |         } else { // n.getChildCount() == 3
776 |           Node decl = n.getFirstChild();
777 |           Node iter = decl.getNext();
778 |           addAllChildren(decl);
779 |           addAllChildren(iter);
780 |         }
781 |       }
782 | 
783 |       if (parent.getType() == Token.VAR ||
784 |           parent.getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT ||
785 |           parent.getType() == Token.RETURN ||
786 |           parent.getType() == Token.THROW) {
787 |         addSimplifiedExpression(n, parent);
788 |       }
789 | 
790 |       if ((parent.getType() == Token.IF ||
791 |            parent.getType() == Token.WHILE ||
792 |            parent.getType() == Token.WITH ||
793 |            parent.getType() == Token.SWITCH ||
794 |            parent.getType() == Token.CASE) &&
795 |           parent.getFirstChild() == n) {
796 |         addAllChildren(n);
797 |       }
798 | 
799 |       if (parent.getType() == Token.DO && parent.getLastChild() == n) {
800 |         addAllChildren(n);
801 |       }
802 | 
803 |       return true;
804 |     }

===== M0641 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.assignNames(Set<Assignment>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 441-511
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines which new names to substitute for the original names.
   */
Method code:
441 |   private void assignNames(Set<Assignment> varsToRename) {
442 |     NameGenerator globalNameGenerator =
443 |         new NameGenerator(reservedNames, prefix, reservedCharacters);
444 | 
445 |     // Local variables never need a prefix.
446 |     NameGenerator localNameGenerator =
447 |         prefix.isEmpty() ? globalNameGenerator : new NameGenerator(
448 |             reservedNames, "", reservedCharacters);
449 | 
450 |     // Generated names and the assignments for non-local vars.
451 |     List<Assignment> pendingAssignments = new ArrayList<Assignment>();
452 |     List<String> generatedNamesForAssignments = new ArrayList<String>();
453 | 
454 |     for (Assignment a : varsToRename) {
455 |       if (a.newName != null) {
456 |         continue;
457 |       }
458 | 
459 |       if (externNames.contains(a.oldName)) {
460 |         continue;
461 |       }
462 | 
463 |       String newName;
464 |       if (a.oldName.startsWith(LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX)) {
465 |         // For local variable, we make the assignment right away.
466 |         newName = localNameGenerator.generateNextName();
467 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, newName);
468 |       } else {
469 |         // For non-local variable, delay finalizing the name assignment
470 |         // until we know how many new names we'll have of length 2, 3, etc.
471 |         newName = globalNameGenerator.generateNextName();
472 |         pendingAssignments.add(a);
473 |         generatedNamesForAssignments.add(newName);
474 |       }
475 |       reservedNames.add(newName);
476 |     }
477 | 
478 |     // Now that we have a list of generated names, and a list of variable
479 |     // Assignment objects, we assign the generated names to the vars as
480 |     // follows:
481 |     // 1) The most frequent vars get the shorter names.
482 |     // 2) If N number of vars are going to be assigned names of the same
483 |     //    length, we assign the N names based on the order at which the vars
484 |     //    first appear in the source. This makes the output somewhat less
485 |     //    random, because symbols declared close together are assigned names
486 |     //    that are quite similar. With this heuristic, the output is more
487 |     //    compressible.
488 |     //    For instance, the output may look like:
489 |     //    var da = "..", ea = "..";
490 |     //    function fa() { .. } function ga() { .. }
491 | 
492 |     int numPendingAssignments = generatedNamesForAssignments.size();
493 |     for (int i = 0; i < numPendingAssignments;) {
494 |       SortedSet<Assignment> varsByOrderOfOccurrence =
495 |           new TreeSet<Assignment>(ORDER_OF_OCCURRENCE_COMPARATOR);
496 | 
497 |       // Add k number of Assignment to the set, where k is the number of
498 |       // generated names of the same length.
499 |       int len = generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i).length();
500 |       for (int j = i; j < numPendingAssignments
501 |           && generatedNamesForAssignments.get(j).length() == len; j++) {
502 |         varsByOrderOfOccurrence.add(pendingAssignments.get(j));
503 |       }
504 | 
505 |       // Now, make the assignments
506 |       for (Assignment a : varsByOrderOfOccurrence) {
507 |         finalizeNameAssignment(a, generatedNamesForAssignments.get(i));
508 |         ++i;
509 |       }
510 |     }

470 |   private void traverseFunction(Node n, Node parent) {
471 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 3);
472 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION);
473 | 
474 |     final Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
475 | 
476 |     boolean isFunctionExpression = (parent != null)
477 |         && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n);
478 | 
479 |     if (!isFunctionExpression) {
480 |       // Functions declarations are in the scope containing the declaration.
481 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
482 |     }
483 | 
484 |     curNode = n;
485 |     pushScope(n);
486 | 
487 |     if (isFunctionExpression) {
488 |       // Function expression names are only accessible within the function
489 |       // scope.
490 |       traverseBranch(fnName, n);
491 |     }
492 | 
493 |     final Node args = fnName.getNext();
494 |     final Node body = args.getNext();
495 | 
496 |     // Args
497 |     traverseBranch(args, n);
498 | 
499 |     // Body
500 |     Preconditions.checkState(body.getNext() == null &&
501 |             body.getType() == Token.BLOCK);
502 |     traverseBranch(body, n);
503 | 
504 |     popScope();

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node)

Original range: 1244-1292
Documentation:
/**
   * Replaces a new Array or Object node with an object literal, unless the
   * call to Array or Object is to a local function with the same name.
   */
Method code:
1244 |   private Node tryFoldLiteralConstructor(Node n) {
1245 |     Preconditions.checkArgument(n.getType() == Token.CALL
1246 |         || n.getType() == Token.NEW);
1247 | 
1248 |     Node constructorNameNode = n.getFirstChild();
1249 | 
1250 |     Node newLiteralNode = null;
1251 | 
1252 |     // We require the AST to be normalized to ensure that, say,
1253 |     // Object() really refers to the built-in Object constructor
1254 |     // and not a user-defined constructor with the same name.
1255 | 
1256 |     if (isASTNormalized() && Token.NAME == constructorNameNode.getType()) {
1257 | 
1258 |       String className = constructorNameNode.getString();
1259 | 
1260 |       if ("RegExp".equals(className)) {
1261 |         // "RegExp("boo", "g")" --> /boo/g
1262 |         return tryFoldRegularExpressionConstructor(n);
1263 |       } else {
1264 |         boolean constructorHasArgs = constructorNameNode.getNext() != null;
1265 | 
1266 |         if ("Object".equals(className) && !constructorHasArgs) {
1267 |           // "Object()" --> "{}"
1268 |           newLiteralNode = new Node(Token.OBJECTLIT);
1269 |         } else if ("Array".equals(className)) {
1270 |           // "Array(arg0, arg1, ...)" --> "[arg0, arg1, ...]"
1271 |           Node arg0 = constructorNameNode.getNext();
1272 |           FoldArrayAction action = isSafeToFoldArrayConstructor(arg0);
1273 | 
1274 |           if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS ||
1275 |               action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITHOUT_ARGS) {
1276 |             newLiteralNode = new Node(Token.ARRAYLIT);
1277 |             n.removeChildren();
1278 |             if (action == FoldArrayAction.SAFE_TO_FOLD_WITH_ARGS) {
1279 |               newLiteralNode.addChildrenToFront(arg0);
1280 |             }
1281 |           }
1282 |         }
1283 | 
1284 |         if (newLiteralNode != null) {
1285 |           n.getParent().replaceChild(n, newLiteralNode);
1286 |           reportCodeChange();
1287 |           return newLiteralNode;
1288 |         }
1289 |       }
1290 |     }
1291 |     return n;
1292 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.toSource(CodeBuilder,int,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java

Documentation:
/**
   * Writes out js code from a root node. If printing input delimiters, this
   * method will attach a comment to the start of the text indicating which
   * input the output derived from. If there were any preserve annotations
   * within the root's source, they will also be printed in a block comment
   * at the beginning of the output.
   */
Method code:
1399 |   public void toSource(final CodeBuilder cb,
1400 |                        final int inputSeqNum,
1401 |                        final Node root) {
1402 |     runInCompilerThread(new Callable<Void>() {
1403 |       public Void call() throws Exception {
1404 |         if (options.printInputDelimiter) {
1405 |           if ((cb.getLength() > 0) && !cb.endsWith("\n")) {
1406 |             cb.append("\n");  // Make sure that the label starts on a new line
1407 |           }
1408 |           Preconditions.checkState(root.getType() == Token.SCRIPT);
1409 | 
1410 |           String delimiter = options.inputDelimiter;
1411 | 
1412 |           String sourceName = root.getSourceFileName();
1413 |           Preconditions.checkState(sourceName != null);
1414 |           Preconditions.checkState(!sourceName.isEmpty());
1415 | 
1416 |           delimiter = delimiter.replaceAll("%name%", sourceName)
1417 |             .replaceAll("%num%", String.valueOf(inputSeqNum));
1418 | 
1419 |           cb.append(delimiter)
1420 |             .append("\n");
1421 |         }
1422 |         if (root.getJSDocInfo() != null &&
1423 |             root.getJSDocInfo().getLicense() != null) {
1424 |           cb.append("/*\n")
1425 |             .append(root.getJSDocInfo().getLicense())
1426 |             .append("*/\n");
1427 |         }
1428 | 
1429 |         // If there is a valid source map, then indicate to it that the current
1430 |         // root node's mappings are offset by the given string builder buffer.
1431 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null) {
1432 |           sourceMap.setStartingPosition(
1433 |               cb.getLineIndex(), cb.getColumnIndex());
1434 |         }
1435 | 
1436 |         // if LanguageMode is ECMASCRIPT5_STRICT, only print 'use strict'
1437 |         // for the first input file
1438 |         String code = toSource(root, sourceMap, inputSeqNum == 0);
1439 |         if (!code.isEmpty()) {
1440 |           cb.append(code);
1441 | 
1442 |           // In order to avoid parse ambiguity when files are concatenated
1443 |           // together, all files should end in a semi-colon. Do a quick
1444 |           // heuristic check if there's an obvious semi-colon already there.
1445 |           int length = code.length();
1446 |           char lastChar = code.charAt(length - 1);
1447 |           char secondLastChar = length >= 2 ?
1448 |               code.charAt(length - 2) : '\0';
1449 |           boolean hasSemiColon = lastChar == ';' ||
1450 |               (lastChar == '\n' && secondLastChar == ';');
1451 |           if (!hasSemiColon) {
1452 |             cb.append(";");
1453 |           }
1454 |         }
1455 |         return null;
1456 |       }
1457 |     });
1458 |   }

/**
   * We treat this as the unknown type if any of its implicit prototype
   * properties is unknown.
   */
Method code:
472 |   @Override
473 |   public boolean isUnknownType() {
474 |     // If the object is unknown now, check the supertype again,
475 |     // because it might have been resolved since the last check.
476 |     if (unknown) {
477 |       ObjectType implicitProto = getImplicitPrototype();
478 |       if (implicitProto == null ||
479 |           implicitProto.isNativeObjectType()) {
480 |         unknown = false;
481 |         for (ObjectType interfaceType : getCtorExtendedInterfaces()) {
482 |           if (interfaceType.isUnknownType()) {
483 |             unknown = true;

485 |           }
486 |         }
487 |       } else {
488 |         unknown = implicitProto.isUnknownType();
489 |       }
490 |     }
491 |     return unknown;
492 |   }

   * Query the DefinitionProvider for the list of definitions that
   * correspond to a given qualified name subtree.  Return null if
   * DefinitionProvider does not contain an entry for a given name,
   * one or more of the values returned by getDeclarations is not
   * callable, or the "name" node is not a GETPROP or NAME.

Method code:
189 |   private static Collection<Definition> getCallableDefinitions(

192 |       List<Definition> result = Lists.newArrayList();
193 | 
194 |       Collection<Definition> decls =
195 |           definitionProvider.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(name);

/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AbstractCommandLineRunner.writeOutput(Appendable,Compiler,String,String,String)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AbstractCommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 565-596
Documentation:
/**
   * Writes code to an output stream, optionally wrapping it in an arbitrary
   * wrapper that contains a placeholder where the code should be inserted.
   */
Method code:
565 |   static void writeOutput(Appendable out, Compiler compiler, String code,
566 |       String wrapper, String codePlaceholder) throws IOException {
567 |     int pos = wrapper.indexOf(codePlaceholder);
568 |     if (pos != -1) {
569 |       String prefix = "";
570 | 
571 |       if (pos > 0) {
572 |         prefix = wrapper.substring(0, pos);
573 |         out.append(prefix);
574 |       }
575 | 
576 |       out.append(code);
577 | 
578 |       int suffixStart = pos + codePlaceholder.length();
579 |       if (suffixStart != wrapper.length()) {
580 |         // Something after placeholder?
581 |         out.append(wrapper.substring(suffixStart));
582 |       }
583 |       // Make sure we always end output with a line feed.
584 |       out.append('\n');
585 | 
586 |       // If we have a source map, adjust its offsets to match
587 |       // the code WITHIN the wrapper.
588 |       if (compiler != null && compiler.getSourceMap() != null) {
589 |         compiler.getSourceMap().setWrapperPrefix(prefix);
590 |       }
591 | 
592 |     } else {
593 |       out.append(code);
594 |       out.append('\n');
595 |     }
596 |   }

Method code:
541 |   private boolean isSimpleAssignment(Node n) {
542 |     // For our purposes we define a simple assignment to be a assignment

544 |     if (NodeUtil.isExprAssign(n)

===== M0715 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryReplaceIf(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 234-271
Documentation:
/**
   * Use "return x?1:2;" in place of "if(x)return 1;return 2;"
   */
Method code:
234 |   private Node tryReplaceIf(Node n) {
235 | 
236 |     for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
237 |          child != null; child = child.getNext()){
238 |       if (child.getType() == Token.IF){
239 | 
240 |         Node cond = child.getFirstChild();
241 |         Node thenBranch = cond.getNext();
242 |         Node elseBranch = thenBranch.getNext();
243 |         Node nextNode = child.getNext();
244 | 
245 |         if (nextNode != null && elseBranch == null &&
246 |             isReturnBlock(thenBranch) && isReturnExpression(nextNode)) {
247 |           Node thenExpr = null;
248 |           // if(x)return; return 1 -> return x?void 0:1
249 |           if (isReturnExpressBlock(thenBranch)) {
250 |             thenExpr = getBlockReturnExpression(thenBranch);
251 |             thenExpr.detachFromParent();
252 |           } else {
253 |             thenExpr = NodeUtil.newUndefinedNode(child);
254 |           }
255 | 
256 |           Node elseExpr = nextNode.getFirstChild();
257 | 
258 |           cond.detachFromParent();
259 |           elseExpr.detachFromParent();
260 | 
261 |           Node hookNode = new Node(Token.HOOK, cond, thenExpr, elseExpr)
262 |                               .copyInformationFrom(child);
263 |           Node returnNode = new Node(Token.RETURN, hookNode);
264 |           n.replaceChild(child, returnNode);
265 |           n.removeChild(nextNode);
266 |           reportCodeChange();
267 |         }
268 |       }
269 |     }
270 |     return n;
271 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InlineVariables.InliningBehavior.isVarInlineForbidden(Var)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InlineVariables.java
Original range: 344-355
Documentation:
/**
     * Whether the given variable is forbidden from being inlined.
     */
Method code:
344 |     private boolean isVarInlineForbidden(Var var) {
345 |       // A variable may not be inlined if:
346 |       // 1) The variable is exported,
347 |       // 2) A reference to the variable has been inlined. We're downstream
348 |       //    of the mechanism that creates variable references, so we don't
349 |       //    have a good way to update the reference. Just punt on it.
350 |       // 3) Don't inline the special RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME
351 |       return var.isExtern()
352 |           || compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(var.name)
353 |           || RenameProperties.RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(var.name)
354 |           || staleVars.contains(var);
355 |     }

===== M0749 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AnalyzePrototypeProperties.ProcessProperties.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AnalyzePrototypeProperties.java
Original range: 220-286
Documentation:

Method code:
220 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
221 |       if (n.getType() == Token.GETPROP) {
222 |         String propName = n.getFirstChild().getNext().getString();
223 |         if (propName.equals("prototype")) {
224 |           processPrototypeParent(t, parent);
225 |         } else if (compiler.getCodingConvention().isExported(propName)) {
226 |           addGlobalUseOfSymbol(propName, t.getModule(), PROPERTY);
227 |         } else {
228 |           addSymbolUse(propName, t.getModule(), PROPERTY);
229 |         }
230 |       } else if (n.getType() == Token.OBJECTLIT &&
231 |           // Make sure that we're not handling object literals being
232 |           // assigned to a prototype, as in:
233 |           // Foo.prototype = {bar: 3, baz: 5};
234 |           !(parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
235 |             parent.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.GETPROP &&
236 |             parent.getFirstChild().getLastChild().getString().equals(
237 |                 "prototype"))) {
238 |         // var x = {a: 1, b: 2}
239 |         // should count as a use of property a and b.
240 |         for (Node propNameNode = n.getFirstChild(); propNameNode != null;
241 |              propNameNode = propNameNode.getNext()) {
242 |           // May be STRING, GET, or SET, but NUMBER isn't interesting.
243 |           if (!propNameNode.isQuotedString()) {
244 |             addSymbolUse(propNameNode.getString(), t.getModule(), PROPERTY);
245 |           }
246 |         }
247 |       } else if (n.getType() == Token.NAME) {
248 |         String name = n.getString();
249 | 
250 |         Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
251 |         if (var != null) {
252 |           // Only process global functions.
253 |           if (var.isGlobal()) {
254 |             if (var.getInitialValue() != null &&
255 |                 var.getInitialValue().getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
256 |               if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
257 |                 if (!processGlobalFunctionDeclaration(t, n, parent,
258 |                         parent.getParent())) {
259 |                   addGlobalUseOfSymbol(name, t.getModule(), VAR);
260 |                 }
261 |               } else {
262 |                 addSymbolUse(name, t.getModule(), VAR);
263 |               }
264 |             }
265 | 
266 |           // If it is not a global, it might be accessing a local of the outer
267 |           // scope. If that's the case the functions between the variable's
268 |           // declaring scope and the variable reference scope cannot be moved.
269 |           } else if (var.getScope() != t.getScope()){
270 |             for (int i = symbolStack.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
271 |               NameContext context = symbolStack.get(i);
272 |               context.name.readClosureVariables = true;
273 |               if (context.scope == var.getScope()) {
274 |                 break;
275 |               }
276 |             }
277 |           }
278 |         }
279 |       }
280 | 
281 |       if (isPrototypePropertyAssign(n) ||
282 |           isGlobalFunctionDeclaration(t, n) ||
283 |           NodeUtil.isFunction(n)) {
284 |         symbolStack.pop();
285 |       }
286 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldBinaryOperator(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java
Original range: 86-153
Documentation:

Method code:
86 |   private Node tryFoldBinaryOperator(Node subtree) {
87 |     Node left = subtree.getFirstChild();
88 | 
89 |     if (left == null) {
90 |       return subtree;
91 |     }
92 | 
93 |     Node right = left.getNext();
94 | 
95 |     if (right == null) {
96 |       return subtree;
97 |     }
98 | 
99 |     // If we've reached here, node is truly a binary operator.
100 |     switch(subtree.getType()) {
101 |       case Token.GETPROP:
102 |         return tryFoldGetProp(subtree, left, right);
103 | 
104 |       case Token.GETELEM:
105 |         return tryFoldGetElem(subtree, left, right);
106 | 
107 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
108 |         return tryFoldInstanceof(subtree, left, right);
109 | 
110 |       case Token.AND:
111 |       case Token.OR:
112 |         return tryFoldAndOr(subtree, left, right);
113 | 
114 |       case Token.LSH:
115 |       case Token.RSH:
116 |       case Token.URSH:
117 |         return tryFoldShift(subtree, left, right);
118 | 
119 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
120 |         return tryFoldAssign(subtree, left, right);
121 | 
122 |       case Token.ADD:
123 |         return tryFoldAdd(subtree, left, right);
124 | 
125 |       case Token.SUB:
126 |       case Token.DIV:
127 |       case Token.MOD:
128 |         return tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
129 | 
130 |       case Token.MUL:
131 |       case Token.BITAND:
132 |       case Token.BITOR:
133 |       case Token.BITXOR:
134 |         Node result = tryFoldArithmeticOp(subtree, left, right);
135 |         if (result != subtree) {
136 |           return result;
137 |         }
138 |         return tryFoldLeftChildOp(subtree, left, right);
139 | 
140 |       case Token.LT:
141 |       case Token.GT:
142 |       case Token.LE:
143 |       case Token.GE:
144 |       case Token.EQ:
145 |       case Token.NE:
146 |       case Token.SHEQ:
147 |       case Token.SHNE:
148 |         return tryFoldComparison(subtree, left, right);
149 | 
150 |       default:
151 |         return subtree;
152 |     }
153 |   }

243 | 
244 |       // Create a map of references to defines keyed by node for easy lookup
245 |       allRefInfo = Maps.newHashMap();
246 |       for (Name name : listOfDefines) {
247 |         if (name.declaration != null) {
248 |           allRefInfo.put(name.declaration.node,
249 |                          new RefInfo(name.declaration, name));
250 |         }
251 |         for (Ref ref : name.getRefs()) {
252 |           if (ref == name.declaration) {
253 |             // Declarations were handled above.
254 |             continue;
255 |           }
256 | 
257 |           // If there's a TWIN def, only put one of the twins in.
258 |           if (ref.getTwin() == null || !ref.getTwin().isSet()) {

260 |           }
261 |         }
262 |       }

Method code:
482 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
483 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
484 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
485 |     if (node.getType() == Token.BLOCK && parent != null &&
486 |         parent.getType() == Token.TRY &&
487 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
488 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
489 |       return;
490 |     }
491 | 
492 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
493 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
494 | 
495 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
496 |     // function (unless it is called)
497 |     while (child != null && child.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
498 |       child = child.getNext();
499 |     }
500 | 
501 |     if (child != null) {
502 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
503 |     } else {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
505 |     }
506 | 
507 |     // Synthetic blocks
508 |     if (parent != null) {
509 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
510 |         case Token.DEFAULT:
511 |         case Token.CASE:
512 |         case Token.TRY:
513 |           break;
514 |         default:
515 |           if (node.getType() == Token.BLOCK && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
516 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));
517 |           }
518 |           break;
519 |       }
520 |     }

213 |     @Override
214 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
215 |       if (n.getType() != Token.NAME) {
216 |         return;
217 |       }
218 | 
219 |       String name = n.getString();
220 | 
221 |       // Ignore anonymous functions
222 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
223 |         return;
224 |       }
225 | 
226 |       // Is this local or Global?
227 |       // Bleeding functions should be treated as part of their outer
228 |       // scope, because IE has bugs in how it handles bleeding
229 |       // functions.
230 |       Scope.Var var = t.getScope().getVar(name);
231 |       boolean local = (var != null) && var.isLocal() &&
232 |           (!var.scope.getParent().isGlobal() ||
233 |            !var.isBleedingFunction());
234 | 
235 |       // Are we renaming global variables?
236 |       if (!local && localRenamingOnly) {
237 |         reservedNames.add(name);
238 |         return;
239 |       }
240 | 
241 |       // Are we renaming function expression names?
242 |       if (preserveFunctionExpressionNames && var != null
243 |           && NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(var.getParentNode())) {
244 |         reservedNames.add(name);
245 |         return;
246 |       }
247 | 
248 |       // Check if we can rename this.
249 |       if (!okToRenameVar(name, local)) {
250 |         if (local) {
251 |           // Blindly de-uniquify for the Prototype library for issue 103.
252 |           String newName = MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.ContextualRenameInverter
253 |               .getOrginalName(name);
254 |           if (!newName.equals(name)) {
255 |             n.setString(newName);
256 |           }
257 |         }
258 |         return;
259 |       }
260 | 
261 |       if (isExternsPass_) {
262 |         // Keep track of extern globals.
263 |         if (!local) {
264 |           externNames.add(name);
265 |         }
266 |         return;
267 |       }
268 | 
269 |       if (pseudoNameMap != null) {
270 |         recordPseudoName(n);
271 |       }
272 | 
273 |       if (local) {
274 |         // Local var: assign a new name
275 |         String tempName = LOCAL_VAR_PREFIX + getLocalVarIndex(var);
276 |         incCount(tempName);
277 |         localNameNodes.add(n);
278 |         n.setString(tempName);
279 |       } else if (var != null) { // Not an extern
280 |         // If it's global, increment global count
281 |         incCount(name);
282 |         globalNameNodes.add(n);
283 |       }
284 |     }

730 |   @Override

755 |         this.call.isEquivalentTo(that.call);

===== M0853 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.BasicErrorManager.LeveledJSErrorComparator.compare(ErrorWithLevel,ErrorWithLevel)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/BasicErrorManager.java
Original range: 120-170
Documentation:

Method code:
120 |     public int compare(ErrorWithLevel p1, ErrorWithLevel p2) {
121 |       // null is the smallest value
122 |       if (p2 == null) {
123 |         if (p1 == null) {
124 |           return 0;
125 |         } else {
126 |           return P1_GT_P2;
127 |         }
128 |       }
129 | 
130 |       // check level
131 |       if (p1.level != p2.level) {
132 |         return p2.level.compareTo(p1.level);
133 |       }
134 | 
135 |       // sourceName comparison
136 |       String source1 = p1.error.sourceName;
137 |       String source2 = p2.error.sourceName;
138 |       if (source1 != null && source2 != null) {
139 |         int sourceCompare = source1.compareTo(source2);
140 |         if (sourceCompare != 0) {
141 |           return sourceCompare;
142 |         }
143 |       } else if (source1 == null && source2 != null) {
144 |         return P1_LT_P2;
145 |       } else if (source1 != null && source2 == null) {
146 |         return P1_GT_P2;
147 |       }
148 |       // lineno comparison
149 |       int lineno1 = p1.error.lineNumber;
150 |       int lineno2 = p2.error.lineNumber;
151 |       if (lineno1 != lineno2) {
152 |         return lineno1 - lineno2;
153 |       } else if (lineno1 < 0 && 0 <= lineno2) {
154 |         return P1_LT_P2;
155 |       } else if (0 <= lineno1 && lineno2 < 0) {
156 |         return P1_GT_P2;
157 |       }
158 |       // charno comparison
159 |       int charno1 = p1.error.getCharno();
160 |       int charno2 = p2.error.getCharno();
161 |       if (charno1 != charno2) {
162 |         return charno1 - charno2;
163 |       } else if (charno1 < 0 && 0 <= charno2) {
164 |         return P1_LT_P2;
165 |       } else if (0 <= charno1 && charno2 < 0) {
166 |         return P1_GT_P2;
167 |       }
168 |       // description
169 |       return p1.error.description.compareTo(p2.error.description);
170 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeParameters.canChangeSignature(DefinitionSite,SimpleDefinitionFinder)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeParameters.java
Original range: 84-146
Documentation:
/**
   * @return Whether the definitionSite represents a function whose call
   *      signature can be modified.
   */
Method code:
84 |   private boolean canChangeSignature(
85 |       DefinitionSite definitionSite, SimpleDefinitionFinder defFinder) {
86 |     Definition definition = definitionSite.definition;
87 | 
88 |     if (definitionSite.inExterns) {
89 |       return false;
90 |     }
91 | 
92 |     // Only functions may be rewritten.
93 |     // Functions that access "arguments" are not eligible since
94 |     // rewrite changes the structure of this object.
95 |     Node rValue = definition.getRValue();
96 |     if (rValue == null ||
97 |         !NodeUtil.isFunction(rValue) ||
98 |         NodeUtil.isVarArgsFunction(rValue)) {
99 |       return false;
100 |     }
101 | 
102 |     // TODO(johnlenz): support rewriting methods defined as part of
103 |     // object literals (they are generally problematic because they may be
104 |     // maps of functions use in for-in expressions, etc).
105 |     // Be conservative, don't try to optimize any declaration that isn't as
106 |     // simple function declaration or assignment.
107 |     if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isSimpleFunctionDeclaration(rValue)) {
108 |       return false;
109 |     }
110 | 
111 |     // Assume an exported method result is used.
112 |     if (!defFinder.canModifyDefinition(definition)) {
113 |       return false;
114 |     }
115 | 
116 |     Collection<UseSite> useSites = defFinder.getUseSites(definition);
117 | 
118 |     if (useSites.isEmpty()) {
119 |       return false;
120 |     }
121 | 
122 |     for (UseSite site : useSites) {
123 |       // Any non-call reference maybe introducing an alias. Don't try to
124 |       // change the function signature, if all the aliases can't also be
125 |       // changed.
126 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Support .call signature changes.
127 |       if (!SimpleDefinitionFinder.isCallOrNewSite(site)) {
128 |         return false;
129 |       }
130 | 
131 |       // TODO(johnlenz): support specialization
132 | 
133 |       // Multiple definitions prevent rewrite.
134 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Allow rewrite all definitions are valid.
135 |       Node nameNode = site.node;
136 |       Collection<Definition> singleSiteDefinitions =
137 |           defFinder.getDefinitionsReferencedAt(nameNode);
138 |       if (singleSiteDefinitions.size() > 1) {
139 |         return false;
140 |       }
141 |       Preconditions.checkState(!singleSiteDefinitions.isEmpty());
142 |       Preconditions.checkState(singleSiteDefinitions.contains(definition));
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     return true;
146 |   }

===== M0907 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 120-163
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the boolean value of a node that represents a literal. This method
   * effectively emulates the <code>Boolean()</code> JavaScript cast function
   * except it return UNKNOWN for known values with side-effects, use
   * getExpressionBooleanValue if you don't care about side-effects.
   */
Method code:
120 |   static TernaryValue getPureBooleanValue(Node n) {
121 |     switch (n.getType()) {
122 |       case Token.STRING:
123 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getString().length() > 0);
124 | 
125 |       case Token.NUMBER:
126 |         return TernaryValue.forBoolean(n.getDouble() != 0);
127 | 
128 |       case Token.NOT:
129 |         return getPureBooleanValue(n.getLastChild()).not();
130 | 
131 |       case Token.NULL:
132 |       case Token.FALSE:
133 |         return TernaryValue.FALSE;
134 | 
135 |       case Token.VOID:
136 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
137 | 
138 |       case Token.NAME:
139 |         String name = n.getString();
140 |         if ("undefined".equals(name)
141 |             || "NaN".equals(name)) {
142 |           // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
143 |           // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
144 |           return TernaryValue.FALSE;
145 |         } else if ("Infinity".equals(name)) {
146 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
147 |         }
148 |         break;
149 | 
150 |       case Token.TRUE:
151 |       case Token.REGEXP:
152 |         return TernaryValue.TRUE;
153 | 
154 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
155 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
156 |         if (!mayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
157 |           return TernaryValue.TRUE;
158 |         }
159 |         break;
160 |     }
161 | 
162 |     return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
163 |   }

956 |   String jsString(String s) {
957 |     int singleq = 0, doubleq = 0;
958 | 
959 |     // could count the quotes and pick the optimal quote character
960 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
961 |       switch (s.charAt(i)) {

963 |         case '\'': singleq++; break;
964 |       }
965 |     }
966 |

970 |       // more double quotes so escape the single quotes

974 |     } else {
975 |       // more single quotes so escape the doubles
976 |       quote = '\"';
977 |       doublequote = "\\\"";

979 |     }
980 | 
981 |     return strEscape(s, quote, doublequote, singlequote, "\\\\",
982 |         outputCharsetEncoder);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(Node)

Original range: 478-501

/**
   * Returns true if this is an immutable value.
   */
Method code:
478 |   static boolean isImmutableValue(Node n) {
479 |     switch (n.getType()) {
480 |       case Token.STRING:
481 |       case Token.NUMBER:
482 |       case Token.NULL:
483 |       case Token.TRUE:
484 |       case Token.FALSE:
485 |         return true;
486 |       case Token.NOT:
487 |         return isImmutableValue(n.getFirstChild());
488 |       case Token.VOID:
489 |       case Token.NEG:
490 |         return isImmutableValue(n.getFirstChild());
491 |       case Token.NAME:
492 |         String name = n.getString();
493 |         // We assume here that programs don't change the value of the keyword
494 |         // undefined to something other than the value undefined.
495 |         return "undefined".equals(name)
496 |             || "Infinity".equals(name)
497 |             || "NaN".equals(name);
498 |     }
499 | 
500 |     return false;
501 |   }

/**
   * Initialize the compiler options. Only necessary if you're not doing
   * a normal compile() job.
   */
Method code:
226 |   public void initOptions(CompilerOptions options) {
227 |     this.options = options;
228 |     if (errorManager == null) {
229 |       if (outStream == null) {
230 |         setErrorManager(
231 |             new LoggerErrorManager(createMessageFormatter(), logger));
232 |       } else {
233 |         PrintStreamErrorManager printer =
234 |             new PrintStreamErrorManager(createMessageFormatter(), outStream);
235 |         printer.setSummaryDetailLevel(options.summaryDetailLevel);
236 |         setErrorManager(printer);
237 |       }

239 | 
240 |     // DiagnosticGroups override the plain checkTypes option.
241 |     if (options.enables(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_TYPES)) {
242 |       options.checkTypes = true;
243 |     } else if (options.disables(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_TYPES)) {
244 |       options.checkTypes = false;
245 |     } else if (!options.checkTypes) {
246 |       // If DiagnosticGroups did not override the plain checkTypes
247 |       // option, and checkTypes is enabled, then turn off the
248 |       // parser type warnings.

251 |               RhinoErrorReporter.TYPE_PARSE_ERROR),
252 |           CheckLevel.OFF);

256 |       options.setWarningLevel(
257 |           DiagnosticGroups.GLOBAL_THIS,
258 |           options.checkGlobalThisLevel);

262 |       options.setWarningLevel(
263 |           DiagnosticGroups.ES5_STRICT,
264 |           CheckLevel.ERROR);
265 |     }

268 |     List<WarningsGuard> guards = Lists.newArrayList();

272 |     guards.add(options.getWarningsGuard());

275 |

278 |     // checks the externs file for validity. If you don't want to warn
279 |     // about missing variable declarations, we shut that specific

===== M0937 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 496-543
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
496 |     private void extractForInitializer(
497 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
498 | 
499 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
500 |         next = c.getNext();
501 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
502 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
503 |         switch (c.getType()) {
504 |           case Token.LABEL:
505 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
506 |             break;
507 |           case Token.FOR:
508 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
509 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
510 |               if (first.getType() == Token.VAR) {
511 |                 // Transform:
512 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
513 |                 // to:
514 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
515 |                 Node newStatement = first;
516 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
517 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
518 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
519 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
520 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
521 |               }
522 |             } else if (c.getFirstChild().getType() != Token.EMPTY) {
523 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
524 |               Node empty = new Node(Token.EMPTY);
525 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
526 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
527 | 
528 |               Node newStatement;
529 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
530 |               // but are handled differently.
531 |               if (init.getType() == Token.VAR) {
532 |                 newStatement = init;
533 |               } else {
534 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
535 |               }
536 | 
537 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
538 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
539 |             }
540 |             break;
541 |         }
542 |       }
543 |     }

169 |   @Override
170 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
171 |     switch (n.getType()) {
172 |       case Token.CALL:

177 |           if (name.getType() == Token.NAME &&
178 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
179 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
180 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
181 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
182 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
183 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
184 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
185 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
186 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
187 |               break;
188 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
189 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
190 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
191 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
192 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
193 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
194 |               if (arg.getType() == Token.STRING) {
195 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
196 |                 if (dot == -1) {
197 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
198 |                 } else {
199 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
200 |                 }
201 |               }
202 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
203 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
204 |               List<String> typeDecls =
205 |                   convention.identifyTypeDeclarationCall(n);
206 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
207 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
208 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
209 |                 }
210 |               }
211 |

213 |               // get compiled out.
214 |               parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newNumber(0));
215 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
216 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
217 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
218 |             }
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 |         break;
222 | 
223 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
224 |       case Token.NAME:
225 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
226 |         // object.

236 |         // error. Hosited functions will explode if the're provided.

Original range: 56-103

Method code:
56 |   @Override
57 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
58 |     List<Reducer> reducers = ImmutableList.of(new ReturnConstantReducer(),
59 |                                               new GetterReducer(),
60 |                                               new SetterReducer(),
61 |                                               new EmptyFunctionReducer(),
62 |                                               new IdentityReducer());
63 | 
64 |     Multimap<Reducer, Reduction> reductionMap = HashMultimap.create();
65 | 
66 |     // Accumulate possible reductions in the reduction multi map.  They
67 |     // will be applied in the loop below.
68 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root,
69 |                            new ReductionGatherer(reducers, reductionMap));
70 | 
71 |     // Apply reductions iff they will provide some savings.
72 |     for (Reducer reducer : reducers) {
73 |       Collection<Reduction> reductions = reductionMap.get(reducer);
74 |       if (reductions.isEmpty()) {
75 |         continue;
76 |       }
77 | 
78 |       Node helperCode = parseHelperCode(reducer);
79 |       if (helperCode == null) {
80 |         continue;
81 |       }
82 | 
83 |       int helperCodeCost = InlineCostEstimator.getCost(helperCode);
84 | 
85 |       // Estimate savings
86 |       int savings = 0;
87 |       for (Reduction reduction : reductions) {
88 |         savings += reduction.estimateSavings();
89 |       }
90 | 
91 |       // Compare estimated savings against the helper cost.  Apply
92 |       // reductions if doing so will result in some savings.
93 |       if (savings > (helperCodeCost + SAVINGS_THRESHOLD)) {
94 |         for (Reduction reduction : reductions) {
95 |           reduction.apply();
96 |         }
97 | 
98 |         Node addingRoot = compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(null);
99 |         addingRoot.addChildrenToFront(helperCode);
100 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
101 |       }
102 |     }
103 |   }

===== M1003 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.OptimizeArgumentsArray.tryReplaceArguments(Scope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/OptimizeArgumentsArray.java
Original range: 178-290
Documentation:
/**
   * Tries to optimize all the arguments array access in this scope by assigning
   * a name to each element.
   *
   * @param scope scope of the function
   * @return true if any modification has been done to the AST
   */
Method code:
178 |   private boolean tryReplaceArguments(Scope scope) {
179 | 
180 |     Node parametersList = scope.getRootNode().getFirstChild().getNext();
181 |     Preconditions.checkState(parametersList.getType() == Token.LP);
182 | 
183 |     // Keep track of rather this function modified the AST and needs to be
184 |     // reported back to the compiler later.
185 |     boolean changed = false;
186 | 
187 |     // Number of parameter that can be accessed without using the arguments
188 |     // array.
189 |     int numNamedParameter = parametersList.getChildCount();
190 | 
191 |     // We want to guess what the highest index that has been access from the
192 |     // arguments array. We will guess that it does not use anything index higher
193 |     // than the named parameter list first until we see other wise.
194 |     int highestIndex = numNamedParameter - 1;
195 | 
196 |     // Iterate through all the references to arguments array in the function to
197 |     // determine the real highestIndex.
198 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
199 | 
200 |       Node getElem = ref.getParent();
201 | 
202 |       // Bail on anything but argument[c] access where c is a constant.
203 |       // TODO(user): We might not need to bail out all the time, there might
204 |       // be more cases that we can cover.
205 |       if (getElem.getType() != Token.GETELEM) {
206 |         return false;
207 |       }
208 | 
209 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
210 | 
211 |       // We have something like arguments[x] where x is not a constant. That
212 |       // means at least one of the access is not known.
213 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
214 |         // TODO(user): Its possible not to give up just yet. The type
215 |         // inference did a 'semi value propagation'. If we know that string
216 |         // is never a subclass of the type of the index. We'd know that
217 |         // it is never 'callee'.
218 |         return false; // Give up.
219 |       }
220 | 
221 |       Node getElemParent = getElem.getParent();
222 |       // When we have argument[0](), replacing it with a() is semantically
223 |       // different if argument[0] is a function call that refers to 'this'
224 |       if (NodeUtil.isCall(getElemParent) &&
225 |           getElemParent.getFirstChild() == getElem) {
226 |         // TODO(user): We can consider using .call() if aliasing that
227 |         // argument allows shorter alias for other arguments.
228 |         return false;
229 |       }
230 | 
231 |       // Replace the highest index if we see an access that has a higher index
232 |       // than all the one we saw before.
233 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
234 |       if (value > highestIndex) {
235 |         highestIndex = value;
236 |       }
237 |     }
238 | 
239 |     // Number of extra arguments we need.
240 |     // For example: function() { arguments[3] } access index 3 so
241 |     // it will need 4 extra named arguments to changed into:
242 |     // function(a,b,c,d) { d }.
243 |     int numExtraArgs = highestIndex - numNamedParameter + 1;
244 | 
245 |     // Temporary holds the new names as string for quick access later.
246 |     String[] argNames = new String[numExtraArgs];
247 | 
248 |     // Insert the formal parameter to the method's signature.
249 |     // Example: function() --> function(r0, r1, r2)
250 |     for (int i = 0; i < numExtraArgs; i++) {
251 |       String name = getNewName();
252 |       argNames[i] = name;
253 |       parametersList.addChildrenToBack(Node.newString(Token.NAME, name));
254 |       changed = true;
255 |     }
256 | 
257 |     // This loop performs the replacement of arguments[x] -> a if x is known.
258 |     for (Node ref : currentArgumentsAccess) {
259 |       Node index = ref.getNext();
260 | 
261 |       // Skip if it is unknown.
262 |       if (index.getType() != Token.NUMBER) {
263 |         continue;
264 |       }
265 |       int value = (int) index.getDouble();
266 | 
267 |       // Unnamed parameter.
268 |       if (value >= numNamedParameter) {
269 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
270 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, argNames[value - numNamedParameter]));
271 |       } else {
272 | 
273 |         // Here, for no apparent reason, the user is accessing a named parameter
274 |         // with arguments[idx]. We can replace it with the actual name for them.
275 |         Node name = parametersList.getFirstChild();
276 | 
277 |         // This is a linear search for the actual name from the signature.
278 |         // It is not necessary to make this fast because chances are the user
279 |         // will not deliberately write code like this.
280 |         for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) {
281 |           name = name.getNext();
282 |         }
283 |         ref.getParent().getParent().replaceChild(ref.getParent(),
284 |             Node.newString(Token.NAME, name.getString()));
285 |       }
286 |       changed = true;
287 |     }
288 | 
289 |     return changed;
290 |   }

294 |             if (valParent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN && name.isSimpleName() &&
295 |                 name.declaration == ref) {

297 |               // before it's declared
298 |               compiler.report(

300 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
301 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,

306 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.

317 |               if (info != null) {

331 |       }

334 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
