405 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
406 |       switch (n.getType()) {
407 |         case Token.GETPROP:
408 |           Node propNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
409 |           if (propNode.getType() == Token.STRING) {
410 |             maybeMarkCandidate(propNode);
411 |           }
412 |           break;
413 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
414 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
415 |             if (!key.isQuotedString()) {
416 |               maybeMarkCandidate(key);
417 |             } else {
418 |               // Ensure that we never rename some other property in a way
419 |               // that could conflict with this quoted key.
420 |               quotedNames.add(key.getString());
421 |             }
422 |           }
423 |           break;
424 |         case Token.GETELEM:
425 |           // If this is a quoted property access (e.g. x['myprop']), we need to
426 |           // ensure that we never rename some other property in a way that
427 |           // could conflict with this quoted name.
428 |           Node child = n.getLastChild();
429 |           if (child != null && child.getType() == Token.STRING) {
430 |             quotedNames.add(child.getString());
431 |           }
432 |           break;
433 |         case Token.CALL:
434 |           // We replace a JSCompiler_renameProperty function call with a string
435 |           // containing the renamed property.
436 |           Node fnName = n.getFirstChild();
437 |           if (fnName.getType() == Token.NAME &&
438 |               RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(fnName.getString())) {
439 |             callNodeToParentMap.put(n, parent);
440 |             countCallCandidates(t, n);
441 |           }
442 |           break;
443 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
444 |           // We eliminate any stub implementations of JSCompiler_renameProperty
445 |           // that we encounter.

447 |             String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
448 |             if (RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(name)) {

450 |                 parent.detachFromParent();

453 |               }

455 |             }

457 |                      RENAME_PROPERTY_FUNCTION_NAME.equals(parent.getString())) {

===== M1061 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RemoveUnusedVars.interpretAssigns()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RemoveUnusedVars.java
Original range: 703-748
Documentation:
/**
   * Look at all the property assigns to all variables.
   * These may or may not count as references. For example,
   *
   * <code>
   * var x = {};
   * x.foo = 3; // not a reference.
   * var y = foo();
   * y.foo = 3; // is a reference.
   * </code>
   *
   * Interpreting assigments could mark a variable as referenced that
   * wasn't referenced before, in order to keep it alive. Because we find
   * references by lazily traversing subtrees, marking a variable as
   * referenced could trigger new traversals of new subtrees, which could
   * find new references.
   *
   * Therefore, this interpretation needs to be run to a fixed point.
   */
Method code:
703 |   private void interpretAssigns() {
704 |     boolean changes = false;
705 |     do {
706 |       changes = false;
707 | 
708 |       // We can't use traditional iterators and iterables for this list,
709 |       // because our lazily-evaluated continuations will modify it while
710 |       // we traverse it.
711 |       for (int current = 0; current < maybeUnreferenced.size(); current++) {
712 |         Var var = maybeUnreferenced.get(current);
713 |         if (referenced.contains(var)) {
714 |           maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
715 |           current--;
716 |         } else {
717 |           boolean assignedToUnknownValue = false;
718 |           boolean hasPropertyAssign = false;
719 | 
720 |           if (var.getParentNode().getType() == Token.VAR &&
721 |               !NodeUtil.isForIn(var.getParentNode().getParent())) {
722 |             Node value = var.getInitialValue();
723 |             assignedToUnknownValue = value != null &&
724 |                 !NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(value, true);
725 |           } else {
726 |             // This was initialized to a function arg or a catch param
727 |             // or a for...in variable.
728 |             assignedToUnknownValue = true;
729 |           }
730 | 
731 |           for (Assign assign : assignsByVar.get(var)) {
732 |             if (assign.isPropertyAssign) {
733 |               hasPropertyAssign = true;
734 |             } else if (!NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(
735 |                 assign.assignNode.getLastChild(), true)) {
736 |               assignedToUnknownValue = true;
737 |             }
738 |           }
739 | 
740 |           if (assignedToUnknownValue && hasPropertyAssign) {
741 |             changes = markReferencedVar(var) || changes;
742 |             maybeUnreferenced.remove(current);
743 |             current--;
744 |           }
745 |         }
746 |       }
747 |     } while (changes);
748 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ReferenceCollectingCallback.isBlockBoundary(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ReferenceCollectingCallback.java
Original range: 197-227
Documentation:
/**
   * @return true if this node marks the start of a new basic block
   */
Method code:
197 |   private static boolean isBlockBoundary(Node n, Node parent) {
198 |     if (parent != null) {
199 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
200 |         case Token.DO:
201 |         case Token.FOR:
202 |         case Token.TRY:
203 |         case Token.WHILE:
204 |         case Token.WITH:
205 |           // NOTE: TRY has up to 3 child blocks:
206 |           // TRY
207 |           //   BLOCK
208 |           //   BLOCK
209 |           //     CATCH
210 |           //   BLOCK
211 |           // Note that there is an explcit CATCH token but no explicit
212 |           // FINALLY token. For simplicity, we consider each BLOCK
213 |           // a separate basic BLOCK.
214 |           return true;
215 |         case Token.AND:
216 |         case Token.HOOK:
217 |         case Token.IF:
218 |         case Token.OR:
219 |           // The first child of a conditional is not a boundary,
220 |           // but all the rest of the children are.
221 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
222 | 
223 |       }
224 |     }
225 | 
226 |     return n.getType() == Token.CASE;
227 |   }

===== M1082 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ScopedAliases.hotSwapScript(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ScopedAliases.java
Original range: 97-136
Documentation:

Method code:
97 |   @Override
98 |   public void hotSwapScript(Node root) {
99 |     Traversal traversal = new Traversal();
100 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, traversal);
101 | 
102 |     if (!traversal.hasErrors()) {
103 | 
104 |       // Apply the aliases.
105 |       for (AliasUsage aliasUsage : traversal.getAliasUsages()) {
106 |         aliasUsage.applyAlias();
107 |       }
108 | 
109 |       // Remove the alias definitions.
110 |       for (Node aliasDefinition : traversal.getAliasDefinitions()) {
111 |         if (aliasDefinition.getParent().getType() == Token.VAR &&
112 |             aliasDefinition.getParent().hasOneChild()) {
113 |           aliasDefinition.getParent().detachFromParent();
114 |         } else {
115 |           aliasDefinition.detachFromParent();
116 |         }
117 |       }
118 | 
119 |       // Collapse the scopes.
120 |       for (Node scopeCall : traversal.getScopeCalls()) {
121 |         Node expressionWithScopeCall = scopeCall.getParent();
122 |         Node scopeClosureBlock = scopeCall.getLastChild().getLastChild();
123 |         scopeClosureBlock.detachFromParent();
124 |         expressionWithScopeCall.getParent().replaceChild(
125 |             expressionWithScopeCall,
126 |             scopeClosureBlock);
127 |         NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(scopeClosureBlock);
128 |       }
129 | 
130 |       if (traversal.getAliasUsages().size() > 0 ||
131 |           traversal.getAliasDefinitions().size() > 0 ||
132 |           traversal.getScopeCalls().size() > 0) {
133 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
134 |       }
135 |     }
136 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.AbstractCommandLineRunner.createDefineOrTweakReplacements(List<String>,CompilerOptions,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/AbstractCommandLineRunner.java
Original range: 1075-1134
Documentation:
/**
   * Create a map of constant names to constant values from a textual
   * description of the map.
   *
   * @param definitions A list of overriding definitions for defines in
   *     the form <name>[=<val>], where <val> is a number, boolean, or
   *     single-quoted string without single quotes.
   */
Method code:
1075 |   @VisibleForTesting
1076 |   static void createDefineOrTweakReplacements(List<String> definitions,
1077 |       CompilerOptions options, boolean tweaks) {
1078 |     // Parse the definitions
1079 |     for (String override : definitions) {
1080 |       String[] assignment = override.split("=", 2);
1081 |       String defName = assignment[0];
1082 | 
1083 |       if (defName.length() > 0) {
1084 |         String defValue = assignment.length == 1 ? "true" : assignment[1];
1085 | 
1086 |         boolean isTrue = defValue.equals("true");
1087 |         boolean isFalse = defValue.equals("false");
1088 |         if (isTrue || isFalse) {
1089 |           if (tweaks) {
1090 |             options.setTweakToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1091 |           } else {
1092 |             options.setDefineToBooleanLiteral(defName, isTrue);
1093 |           }
1094 |           continue;
1095 |         } else if (defValue.length() > 1
1096 |             && ((defValue.charAt(0) == '\'' &&
1097 |                 defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\'')
1098 |                 || (defValue.charAt(0) == '\"' &&
1099 |                     defValue.charAt(defValue.length() - 1) == '\"'))) {
1100 |           // If the value starts and ends with a single quote,
1101 |           // we assume that it's a string.
1102 |           String maybeStringVal =
1103 |               defValue.substring(1, defValue.length() - 1);
1104 |           if (maybeStringVal.indexOf(defValue.charAt(0)) == -1) {
1105 |             if (tweaks) {
1106 |               options.setTweakToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1107 |             } else {
1108 |               options.setDefineToStringLiteral(defName, maybeStringVal);
1109 |             }
1110 |             continue;
1111 |           }
1112 |         } else {
1113 |           try {
1114 |             double value = Double.parseDouble(defValue);
1115 |             if (tweaks) {
1116 |               options.setTweakToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1117 |             } else {
1118 |               options.setDefineToDoubleLiteral(defName, value);
1119 |             }
1120 |             continue;
1121 |           } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
1122 |             // do nothing, it will be caught at the end
1123 |           }
1124 |         }
1125 |       }
1126 | 
1127 |       if (tweaks) {
1128 |         throw new RuntimeException(
1129 |             "--tweak flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1130 |       }
1131 |       throw new RuntimeException(
1132 |           "--define flag syntax invalid: " + override);
1133 |     }
1134 |   }

===== M1098 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.tryMergeBlock(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1815-1832
Documentation:
/**
   * Merge a block with its parent block.
   * @return Whether the block was removed.
   */
Method code:
1815 |   static boolean tryMergeBlock(Node block) {
1816 |     Preconditions.checkState(block.getType() == Token.BLOCK);
1817 |     Node parent = block.getParent();
1818 |     // Try to remove the block if its parent is a block/script or if its
1819 |     // parent is label and it has exactly one child.
1820 |     if (isStatementBlock(parent)) {
1821 |       Node previous = block;
1822 |       while (block.hasChildren()) {
1823 |         Node child = block.removeFirstChild();
1824 |         parent.addChildAfter(child, previous);
1825 |         previous = child;
1826 |       }
1827 |       parent.removeChild(block);
1828 |       return true;
1829 |     } else {
1830 |       return false;
1831 |     }
1832 |   }

===== M1125 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.runCallable(Callable<T>,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 578-629
Documentation:

Method code:
578 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
579 |   static <T> T runCallable(
580 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
581 | 
582 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the jscompiler overflows the stack when running on some
583 |     // large or complex js code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
584 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
585 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
586 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
587 | 
588 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
589 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
590 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
591 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
592 |       public void run() {
593 |         try {
594 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
595 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
596 |           }
597 |           result[0] = callable.call();
598 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
599 |           exception[0] = e;
600 |         } finally {
601 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
602 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
603 |           }
604 |         }
605 |       }
606 |     };
607 | 
608 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
609 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
610 |       th.start();
611 |       while (true) {
612 |         try {
613 |           th.join();
614 |           break;
615 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
616 |           // ignore
617 |         }
618 |       }
619 |     } else {
620 |       runnable.run();
621 |     }
622 | 
623 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
624 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
625 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
626 |     }
627 | 
628 |     return (T) result[0];
629 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.optimizeSubtree(Node)

Original range: 74-162

/**
   * Tries apply our various peephole minimizations on the passed in node.
   */
Method code:
74 |   @Override
75 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
76 |   public Node optimizeSubtree(Node node) {
77 |     switch(node.getType()) {
78 |       case Token.RETURN: {
79 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
80 |         if (result != node) {
81 |           return result;
82 |         }
83 |         result = tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
84 |         if (result != node) {
85 |           return result;
86 |         }
87 |         return tryReduceReturn(node);
88 |       }
89 | 
90 |       case Token.THROW: {
91 |         Node result = tryRemoveRedundantExit(node);
92 |         if (result != node) {
93 |           return result;
94 |         }
95 |         return tryReplaceExitWithBreak(node);
96 |       }
97 | 
98 |       // TODO(johnlenz): Maybe remove redundant BREAK and CONTINUE. Overlaps
99 |       // with MinimizeExitPoints.
100 | 
101 |       case Token.NOT:
102 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
103 |         return tryMinimizeNot(node);
104 | 
105 |       case Token.IF:
106 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
107 |         return tryMinimizeIf(node);
108 | 
109 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
110 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
111 |         return node;
112 | 
113 |       case Token.HOOK:
114 |         tryMinimizeCondition(node.getFirstChild());
115 |         return node;
116 | 
117 |       case Token.WHILE:
118 |       case Token.DO:
119 |         tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
120 |         return node;
121 | 
122 |       case Token.FOR:
123 |         if (!NodeUtil.isForIn(node)) {
124 |           tryMinimizeCondition(NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(node));
125 |         }
126 |         return node;
127 | 
128 | 
129 |       case Token.TRUE:
130 |       case Token.FALSE:
131 |         return reduceTrueFalse(node);
132 | 
133 |       case Token.NEW:
134 |         node = tryFoldStandardConstructors(node);
135 |         if (node.getType() != Token.CALL) {
136 |           return node;
137 |         }
138 |         // Fall through on purpose because tryFoldStandardConstructors() may
139 |         // convert a NEW node into a CALL node
140 |       case Token.CALL:
141 |         Node result =  tryFoldLiteralConstructor(node);
142 |         if (result == node) {
143 |           result = tryFoldImmediateCallToBoundFunction(node);
144 |         }
145 |         return result;
146 | 
147 |       case Token.COMMA:
148 |         return tryFoldComma(node);
149 | 
150 |       case Token.NAME:
151 |         return tryReplaceUndefined(node);
152 | 
153 |       case Token.BLOCK:
154 |         return tryReplaceIf(node);
155 |

===== M1134 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SourceFile.getLine(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SourceFile.java
Original range: 166-201
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the source line for the indicated line number.
   *
   * @param lineNumber the line number, 1 being the first line of the file.
   * @return The line indicated. Does not include the newline at the end
   *     of the file. Returns {@code null} if it does not exist,
   *     or if there was an IO exception.
   */
Method code:
166 |   public String getLine(int lineNumber) {
167 |     String js = "";
168 |     try {
169 |       // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, this is optimized for few warnings.
170 |       // This is probably the right trade-off, but will be slow if there
171 |       // are lots of warnings in one file.
172 |       js = getCode();
173 |     } catch (IOException e) {
174 |       return null;
175 |     }
176 | 
177 |     int pos = 0;
178 |     int startLine = 1;
179 | 
180 |     // If we've saved a previous offset and it's for a line less than the
181 |     // one we're searching for, then start at that point.
182 |     if (lineNumber >= lastLine) {
183 |       pos = lastOffset;
184 |       startLine = lastLine;
185 |     }
186 | 
187 |     for (int n = startLine; n < lineNumber; n++) {
188 |       int nextpos = js.indexOf('\n', pos);
189 |       if (nextpos == -1) {
190 |         return null;
191 |       }
192 |       pos = nextpos + 1;
193 |     }
194 | 
195 |     // Remember this offset for the next search we do.
196 |     lastOffset = pos;
197 |     lastLine = lineNumber;
198 | 
199 |     return (js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1) ? null :
200 |         js.substring(pos, js.indexOf('\n', pos));
201 |   }

/**
     * Determines whether this block is guaranteed to begin executing before
     * the given block does.
     */
Method code:
681 |     boolean provablyExecutesBefore(BasicBlock thatBlock) {
682 |       // If thatBlock is a descendant of this block, and there are no hoisted
683 |       // blocks between them, then this block must start before thatBlock.
684 |       BasicBlock currentBlock;
685 |       for (currentBlock = thatBlock;
686 |            currentBlock != null && currentBlock != this;
687 |            currentBlock = currentBlock.getParent()) {
688 |         if (currentBlock.isHoisted) {
689 |           return false;
690 |         }
691 |       }

694 |         return true;
695 |       }
696 |       if (isGlobalScopeBlock() && thatBlock.isGlobalScopeBlock()) {
697 |         return true;
698 |       }
699 |       return false;
700 |     }

69 |   @Override
70 |   public void enterScope(NodeTraversal t) {
71 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
72 |     // Global scope _SHOULD_ work, however, liveness won't finish without
73 |     // -Xmx1024 in closure. We might have to look at coding conventions for
74 |     // exported variables as well.
75 |     if (scope.isGlobal()) {

97 |     liveness.analyze();

/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
387 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {
388 |       Node ret;
389 |       if (n instanceof Name) {

392 |         ret = transformNumberAsString((NumberLiteral)n);
393 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
394 |       } else {
395 |         ret = transform(n);
396 |         ret.putBooleanProp(Node.QUOTED_PROP, true);
397 |       }
398 |       Preconditions.checkState(ret.getType() == Token.STRING);
399 |       return ret;
400 |     }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
2454 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
2455 |     char LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN = 0x7f;
2456 |     int len = s.length();
2457 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2458 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2459 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2460 |         return false;
2461 |       }
2462 |     }
2463 |     return true;
2464 |   }

Method code:
499 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
500 |       if (!t.inGlobalScope()) {
501 |         return;
502 |       }
503 | 
504 |       if (n.getType() == Token.ASSIGN) {
505 |         Node nameNode = n.getFirstChild();
506 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, nameNode, n);
507 |         if (ns != null) {
508 |           if (parent.getType() == Token.FOR && !NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
509 |             // Patch for assignments that appear in the init,
510 |             // condition or iteration part of a FOR loop.  Without
511 |             // this change, all 3 of those parts try to claim the for
512 |             // loop as their dependency scope.  The last assignment in
513 |             // those three fields wins, which can result in incorrect
514 |             // reference edges between referenced and assigned variables.
515 |             //
516 |             // TODO(user) revisit the dependency scope calculation
517 |             // logic.
518 |             if (parent.getFirstChild().getNext() != n) {
519 |               recordDepScope(n, ns);
520 |             } else {
521 |               recordDepScope(nameNode, ns);
522 |             }
523 |           } else {
524 |             recordDepScope(n, ns);
525 |           }
526 |         }
527 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(n)) {
528 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, n, parent);
529 |         recordDepScope(n, ns);
530 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
531 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, n.getFirstChild(), n);
532 |         recordDepScope(n, ns);
533 |       } else if (NodeUtil.isExprCall(n)) {
534 |         Node callNode = n.getFirstChild();
535 |         Node nameNode = callNode.getFirstChild();
536 |         NameInformation ns = createNameInformation(t, nameNode, callNode);
537 |         if (ns != null && ns.onlyAffectsClassDef) {

===== M1200 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parse()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 176-920
Documentation:
/**
   * Parses a {@link JSDocInfo} object. This parsing method reads all tokens
   * returned by the {@link JsDocTokenStream#getJsDocToken()} method until the
   * {@link JsDocToken#EOC} is returned.
   *
   * @return {@code true} if JSDoc information was correctly parsed,
   *     {@code false} otherwise
   */
Method code:
176 |   boolean parse() {
177 |     int lineno;
178 |     int charno;
179 | 
180 |     // JSTypes are represented as Rhino AST nodes, and then resolved later.
181 |     JSTypeExpression type;
182 | 
183 |     state = State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION;
184 |     skipEOLs();
185 | 
186 |     JsDocToken token = next();
187 | 
188 |     List<ExtendedTypeInfo> extendedTypes = Lists.newArrayList();
189 | 
190 |     // Always record that we have a comment.
191 |     if (jsdocBuilder.shouldParseDocumentation()) {
192 |       ExtractionInfo blockInfo = extractBlockComment(token);
193 |       token = blockInfo.token;
194 |       if (!blockInfo.string.isEmpty()) {
195 |         jsdocBuilder.recordBlockDescription(blockInfo.string);
196 |       }
197 |     } else {
198 |       if (token != JsDocToken.ANNOTATION &&
199 |           token != JsDocToken.EOC) {
200 |         // Mark that there was a description, but don't bother marking
201 |         // what it was.
202 |         jsdocBuilder.recordBlockDescription("");
203 |       }
204 |     }
205 | 
206 |     // Parse the actual JsDoc.
207 |     retry: for (;;) {
208 |       switch (token) {
209 |         case ANNOTATION:
210 |           if (state == State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION) {
211 |             state = State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE;
212 |             lineno = stream.getLineno();
213 |             charno = stream.getCharno();
214 | 
215 |             String annotationName = stream.getString();
216 |             Annotation annotation = annotationNames.get(annotationName);
217 |             if (annotation == null) {
218 |               parser.addParserWarning("msg.bad.jsdoc.tag", annotationName,
219 |                   stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
220 |             } else {
221 |               // Mark the beginning of the annotation.
222 |               jsdocBuilder.markAnnotation(annotationName, lineno, charno);
223 | 
224 |               switch (annotation) {
225 |                 case AUTHOR:
226 |                   if (jsdocBuilder.shouldParseDocumentation()) {
227 |                     ExtractionInfo authorInfo = extractSingleLineBlock();
228 |                     String author = authorInfo.string;
229 | 
230 |                     if (author.length() == 0) {
231 |                       parser.addParserWarning("msg.jsdoc.authormissing",
232 |                           stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
233 |                     } else {
234 |                       jsdocBuilder.addAuthor(author);
235 |                     }
236 |                     token = authorInfo.token;
237 |                   } else {
238 |                     token = eatTokensUntilEOL(token);
239 |                   }
240 |                   continue retry;
241 | 
242 |                 case CONSTANT:
243 |                   if (!jsdocBuilder.recordConstancy()) {
244 |                     parser.addParserWarning("msg.jsdoc.const",
245 |                         stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
246 |                   }
247 |                   token = eatTokensUntilEOL();
248 |                   continue retry;
249 | 
250 |                 case CONSTRUCTOR:
251 |                   if (!jsdocBuilder.recordConstructor()) {
252 |                     if (jsdocBuilder.isInterfaceRecorded()) {
253 |                       parser.addTypeWarning("msg.jsdoc.interface.constructor",
254 |                           stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
255 |                     } else {
256 |                       parser.addTypeWarning("msg.jsdoc.incompat.type",
257 |                           stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
258 |                     }
259 |                   }
260 |                   token = eatTokensUntilEOL();
261 |                   continue retry;
262 | 
263 |                 case DEPRECATED:
264 |                   if (!jsdocBuilder.recordDeprecated()) {
265 |                     parser.addParserWarning("msg.jsdoc.deprecated",
266 |                         stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
267 |                   }
268 | 
269 |                   // Find the reason/description, if any.
270 |                   ExtractionInfo reasonInfo =
271 |                       extractMultilineTextualBlock(token);
272 | 
273 |                   String reason = reasonInfo.string;
274 | 
275 |                   if (reason.length() > 0) {
276 |                     jsdocBuilder.recordDeprecationReason(reason);
277 |                   }
278 | 
279 |                   token = reasonInfo.token;
280 |                   continue retry;
281 | 
282 |                 case INTERFACE:
283 |                   if (!jsdocBuilder.recordInterface()) {
284 |                     if (jsdocBuilder.isConstructorRecorded()) {
285 |                       parser.addTypeWarning("msg.jsdoc.interface.constructor",
286 |                           stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
287 |                     } else {
288 |                       parser.addTypeWarning("msg.jsdoc.incompat.type",
289 |                           stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
290 |                     }
291 |                   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 1929-1931
Documentation:
/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1929 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1930 |     return n.getType() == Token.FUNCTION && !isStatement(n);
1931 |   }

Method code:
185 |   @Override
186 |   public Bind describeFunctionBind(Node n) {
187 |     // It would be nice to be able to identify a fn.bind call
188 |     // but that requires knowing the type of "fn".
189 | 
190 |     if (n.getType() != Token.CALL) {
191 |       return null;
192 |     }
193 | 
194 |     Node callTarget = n.getFirstChild();
195 |     String name = callTarget.getQualifiedName();
196 |     if (name != null) {
197 |       if (name.equals("Function.prototype.bind.call")) {
198 |         // goog.bind(fn, self, args...);
199 |         Node fn = callTarget.getNext();
200 |         if (fn == null) {
201 |           return null;
202 |         }
203 |         Node thisValue = safeNext(fn);
204 |         Node parameters = safeNext(thisValue);
205 |         return new Bind(fn, thisValue, parameters);
206 |       }
207 |     }
208 | 
209 |     if (callTarget.getType() == Token.GETPROP
210 |         && callTarget.getLastChild().getString().equals("bind")
211 |         && callTarget.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
212 |       // (function(){}).bind(self, args...);
213 |       Node fn = callTarget.getFirstChild();
214 |       Node thisValue = callTarget.getNext();
215 |       Node parameters = safeNext(thisValue);
216 |       return new Bind(fn, thisValue, parameters);
217 |     }
218 | 
219 |     return null;
220 |   }

/**
   * @return an {@link Definition} object if the node contains a definition or
   *     {@code null} otherwise.

36 |   static Definition getDefinition(Node n, boolean isExtern) {
37 |     // TODO(user): Since we have parent pointers handy. A lot of constructors
38 |     // can be simplified.
39 | 
40 |     // This logic must match #isDefinitionNode
41 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
42 |     if (parent == null) {
43 |       return null;

46 |     if (NodeUtil.isVarDeclaration(n) && n.hasChildren()) {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.RenameVars.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/RenameVars.java
Original range: 324-384
Documentation:

Method code:
324 |   @Override
325 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
326 |     assignmentLog = new StringBuilder();
327 | 
328 |     // Do variable reference counting.
329 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, externs, new ProcessVars(true));
330 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, new ProcessVars(false));
331 | 
332 |     // Make sure that new names don't overlap with extern names.
333 |     reservedNames.addAll(externNames);
334 | 
335 |     // Rename vars, sorted by frequency of occurrence to minimize code size.
336 |     SortedSet<Assignment> varsByFrequency =
337 |         new TreeSet<Assignment>(FREQUENCY_COMPARATOR);
338 |     varsByFrequency.addAll(assignments.values());
339 | 
340 |     if (shouldShadow) {
341 |       new ShadowVariables(
342 |           compiler, assignments, varsByFrequency, pseudoNameMap).process(
343 |               externs, root);
344 |     }
345 | 
346 |     // First try to reuse names from an earlier compilation.
347 |     if (prevUsedRenameMap != null) {
348 |       reusePreviouslyUsedVariableMap();
349 |     }
350 | 
351 |     // Assign names, sorted by descending frequency to minimize code size.
352 |     assignNames(varsByFrequency);
353 | 
354 |     boolean changed = false;
355 | 
356 |     // Rename the globals!
357 |     for (Node n : globalNameNodes) {
358 |       String newName = getNewGlobalName(n);
359 |       // Note: if newName is null, then oldName is an extern.
360 |       if (newName != null) {
361 |         n.setString(newName);
362 |         changed = true;
363 |       }
364 |     }
365 | 
366 |     // Rename the locals!
367 |     int count = 0;
368 |     for (Node n : localNameNodes) {
369 |       String newName = getNewLocalName(n);
370 |       if (newName != null) {
371 |         n.setString(newName);
372 |         changed = true;
373 |       }
374 |       count++;
375 |     }
376 | 
377 |     if (changed) {
378 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
379 |     }
380 | 
381 |     // Lastly, write the name assignments to the debug log.
382 |     compiler.addToDebugLog("JS var assignments:\n" + assignmentLog);
383 |     assignmentLog = null;
384 |   }

/**
   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.
   * @param silence_threshold Traces for time less than silence_threshold
   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran
   */
Method code:
406 |   long stop(int silence_threshold) {
407 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
408 | 
409 |     ThreadTrace trace = getThreadTrace();
410 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
411 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
412 |       return 0;
413 |     }
414 | 
415 |     stopTimeMs = clock.currentTimeMillis();
416 |     if (extraTracingValues != null) {
417 |       // We use extraTracingValues.length rather than
418 |       // extraTracingStatistics.size() because a new statistic may
419 |       // have been added
420 |       for (int i = 0; i < extraTracingValues.length; i++) {
421 |         long value = extraTracingStatistics.get(i).stop(startThread);
422 |         extraTracingValues[i] = value - extraTracingValues[i];
423 |       }
424 |     }
425 | 
426 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
427 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
428 |       return 0;
429 |     }
430 | 
431 |     trace.endEvent(this, silence_threshold);
432 |     return stopTimeMs - startTimeMs;
433 |   }

   *

1106 |       jsRoot.detachChildren();
1107 |     }
1108 | 
1109 |     // Parse main js sources.
1110 |     jsRoot = new Node(Token.BLOCK);
1111 |     jsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1112 | 
1113 |     externsRoot = new Node(Token.BLOCK);
1114 |     externsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);

1121 |           options.tracer == TracerMode.ALL);

1126 | 
1127 |     try {
1128 |       // Parse externs sources.
1129 |       for (CompilerInput input : externs) {
1130 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1131 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1132 |           return null;
1133 |         }
1134 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1135 |       }

1138 |       if (options.manageClosureDependencies) {

1143 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.

1145 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1146 |           }

1148 | 
1149 |         try {
1150 |           inputs =
1151 |               (moduleGraph == null ? new JSModuleGraph(modules) : moduleGraph)
1152 |               .manageDependencies(
1153 |                   options.manageClosureDependenciesEntryPoints, inputs);
1154 |         } catch (CircularDependencyException e) {
1155 |           report(JSError.make(
1156 |               JSModule.CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1157 |           return null;
1158 |         } catch (MissingProvideException e) {
1159 |           report(JSError.make(
1160 |               MISSING_ENTRY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1161 |           return null;
1162 |         }
1163 |       }
1164 | 
1165 |       // Check if inputs need to be rebuilt from modules.
1166 |       boolean staleInputs = false;
1167 |       for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1168 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1169 | 
1170 |         // Inputs can have a null AST during initial parse.
1171 |         if (n == null) {
1172 |           continue;
1173 |         }
1174 |

1176 |           JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1177 |           if (info.isExterns()) {

1190 |             staleInputs = true;
1191 |           }

1194 |

1203 |         if (n == null) {
1204 |           continue;
1205 |         }
1206 | 
1207 |         if (devMode) {
1208 |           runSanityCheck();

1210 |             return null;
1211 |           }

1215 |             options.nameReferenceReportPath != null) {
1216 |

1218 |           // input file. This information is used to construct the SourceMap.

1223 |         }

1226 |       }
1227 |

1230 |       }

===== M1283 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.tryMinimizeCondition(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax.java
Original range: 1004-1186
Documentation:
/**
   * Try to minimize conditions expressions, as there are additional
   * assumptions that can be made when it is known that the final result
   * is a boolean.
   *
   * The following transformations are done recursively:
   *   !(x||y) --> !x&&!y
   *   !(x&&y) --> !x||!y
   *   !!x     --> x
   * Thus:
   *   !(x&&!y) --> !x||!!y --> !x||y
   *
   *   Returns the replacement for n, or the original if no change was made
   */
Method code:
1004 |   private Node tryMinimizeCondition(Node n) {
1005 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
1006 | 
1007 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1008 |       case Token.NOT:
1009 |         Node first = n.getFirstChild();
1010 |         switch (first.getType()) {
1011 |           case Token.NOT: {
1012 |               Node newRoot = first.removeFirstChild();
1013 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1014 |               reportCodeChange();
1015 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1016 |               // NOT children are handled below.
1017 |               return newRoot;
1018 |             }
1019 |           case Token.AND:
1020 |           case Token.OR: {
1021 |               // !(!x && !y) --> x || y
1022 |               // !(!x || !y) --> x && y
1023 |               // !(!x && y) --> x || !y
1024 |               // !(!x || y) --> x && !y
1025 |               // !(x && !y) --> !x || y
1026 |               // !(x || !y) --> !x && y
1027 |               // !(x && y) --> !x || !y
1028 |               // !(x || y) --> !x && !y
1029 |               Node leftParent = first.getFirstChild();
1030 |               Node rightParent = first.getLastChild();
1031 |               Node left, right;
1032 | 
1033 |               // Check special case when such transformation cannot reduce
1034 |               // due to the added ()
1035 |               // It only occurs when both of expressions are not NOT expressions
1036 |               if (leftParent.getType() != Token.NOT
1037 |                   && rightParent.getType() != Token.NOT) {
1038 |                 // If an expression has higher precendence than && or ||,
1039 |                 // but lower precedence than NOT, an additional () is needed
1040 |                 // Thus we do not preceed
1041 |                 int op_precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType());
1042 |                 if ((isLowerPrecedence(leftParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1043 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(leftParent, op_precedence))
1044 |                     || (isLowerPrecedence(rightParent, NOT_PRECEDENCE)
1045 |                     && isHigherPrecedence(rightParent, op_precedence))) {
1046 |                   return n;
1047 |                 }
1048 |               }
1049 | 
1050 |               if (leftParent.getType() == Token.NOT) {
1051 |                 left = leftParent.removeFirstChild();
1052 |               } else {
1053 |                 leftParent.detachFromParent();
1054 |                 left = new Node(Token.NOT, leftParent)
1055 |                   .copyInformationFrom(leftParent);
1056 |               }
1057 |               if (rightParent.getType() == Token.NOT) {
1058 |                 right = rightParent.removeFirstChild();
1059 |               } else {
1060 |                 rightParent.detachFromParent();
1061 |                 right = new Node(Token.NOT, rightParent)
1062 |                   .copyInformationFrom(rightParent);
1063 |               }
1064 | 
1065 |               int newOp = (first.getType() == Token.AND) ? Token.OR : Token.AND;
1066 |               Node newRoot = new Node(newOp, left, right);
1067 |               parent.replaceChild(n, newRoot);
1068 |               reportCodeChange();
1069 |               // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the
1070 |               // AND and OR children below.
1071 |               return newRoot;
1072 |             }
1073 | 
1074 |            default:
1075 |              TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(first);
1076 |              if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1077 |                boolean result = nVal.not().toBoolean(true);
1078 |                int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1079 |                return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1080 |              }
1081 |         }
1082 |         // No need to traverse, tryMinimizeCondition is called on the NOT
1083 |         // children in the general case in the main post-order traversal.
1084 |         return n;
1085 | 
1086 |       case Token.OR:
1087 |       case Token.AND: {
1088 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
1089 |         Node right = n.getLastChild();
1090 | 
1091 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1092 |         // the children, this can't be done in the general case.
1093 |         left = tryMinimizeCondition(left);
1094 |         right = tryMinimizeCondition(right);
1095 | 
1096 |         // Remove useless conditionals
1097 |         // Handle four cases:
1098 |         //   x || false --> x
1099 |         //   x || true  --> true
1100 |         //   x && true --> x
1101 |         //   x && false  --> false
1102 |         TernaryValue rightVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right);
1103 |         if (NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(right) != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1104 |           int type = n.getType();
1105 |           Node replacement = null;
1106 |           boolean rval = rightVal.toBoolean(true);
1107 | 
1108 |           // (x || FALSE) => x
1109 |           // (x && TRUE) => x
1110 |           if (type == Token.OR && !rval ||
1111 |               type == Token.AND && rval) {
1112 |             replacement = left;
1113 |           } else if (!mayHaveSideEffects(left)) {
1114 |             replacement = right;
1115 |           }
1116 | 
1117 |           if (replacement != null) {
1118 |             n.detachChildren();
1119 |             parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1120 |             reportCodeChange();
1121 |             return replacement;
1122 |           }
1123 |         }
1124 |         return n;
1125 |       }
1126 | 
1127 |       case Token.HOOK: {
1128 |         Node condition = n.getFirstChild();
1129 |         Node trueNode = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
1130 |         Node falseNode = n.getLastChild();
1131 | 
1132 |         // Because the expression is in a boolean context minimize
1133 |         // the result children, this can't be done in the general case.
1134 |         // The condition is handled in the general case in #optimizeSubtree
1135 |         trueNode = tryMinimizeCondition(trueNode);
1136 |         falseNode = tryMinimizeCondition(falseNode);
1137 | 
1138 |         // Handle four cases:
1139 |         //   x ? true : false --> x
1140 |         //   x ? false : true --> !x
1141 |         //   x ? true : y     --> x || y
1142 |         //   x ? y : false    --> x && y
1143 |         Node replacement = null;
1144 |         TernaryValue trueNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(trueNode);
1145 |         TernaryValue falseNodeVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(falseNode);
1146 |         if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE
1147 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1148 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1149 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1150 |           replacement = condition;
1151 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE
1152 |             && falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1153 |           // Remove useless conditionals, keep the condition
1154 |           condition.detachFromParent();
1155 |           replacement = new Node(Token.NOT, condition);
1156 |         } else if (trueNodeVal == TernaryValue.TRUE) {
1157 |           // Remove useless true case.
1158 |           n.detachChildren();
1159 |           replacement = new Node(Token.OR, condition, falseNode);
1160 |         } else if (falseNodeVal == TernaryValue.FALSE) {
1161 |           // Remove useless false case
1162 |           n.detachChildren();
1163 |           replacement = new Node(Token.AND, condition, trueNode);
1164 |         }
1165 | 
1166 |         if (replacement != null) {
1167 |           parent.replaceChild(n, replacement);
1168 |           n = replacement;
1169 |           reportCodeChange();
1170 |         }
1171 | 
1172 |         return n;
1173 |       }
1174 | 
1175 |       default:
1176 |         // while(true) --> while(1)
1177 |         TernaryValue nVal = NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue(n);
1178 |         if (nVal != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
1179 |           boolean result = nVal.toBoolean(true);
1180 |           int equivalentResult = result ? 1 : 0;
1181 |           return maybeReplaceChildWithNumber(n, parent, equivalentResult);
1182 |         }
1183 |         // We can't do anything else currently.
1184 |         return n;
1185 |     }
1186 |   }

===== M1325 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!NodeUtil.isExpressionNode(n) && !NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (NodeUtil.isName(forVar)
85 |           && NodeUtil.isVar(n) && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // Ok, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.getType() == Token.FOR
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().getType() == Token.EMPTY) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some Javascript parsers (such
101 |       // as the Playstation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

===== M1334 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.FixedPointGraphTraversal.computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E>,Set<N>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/graph/FixedPointGraphTraversal.java
Original range: 93-128
Documentation:
/**
   * Compute a fixed point for the given graph, entering from the given nodes.
   * @param graph The graph to traverse.
   * @param entrySet The nodes to begin traversing from.
   */
Method code:
93 |   public void computeFixedPoint(DiGraph<N, E> graph, Set<N> entrySet) {
94 |     int cycleCount = 0;
95 |     long nodeCount = graph.getNodes().size();
96 | 
97 |     // Choose a bail-out heuristically in case the computation
98 |     // doesn't converge.
99 |     long maxIterations = Math.max(nodeCount * nodeCount * nodeCount, 100);
100 | 
101 |     // Use a LinkedHashSet, so that the traversal is deterministic.
102 |     LinkedHashSet<DiGraphNode<N, E>> workSet =
103 |         Sets.newLinkedHashSet();
104 |     for (N n : entrySet) {
105 |       workSet.add(graph.getDirectedGraphNode(n));
106 |     }
107 |     for (; !workSet.isEmpty() && cycleCount < maxIterations; cycleCount++) {
108 |       // For every out edge in the workSet, traverse that edge. If that
109 |       // edge updates the state of the graph, then add the destination
110 |       // node to the resultSet, so that we can update all of its out edges
111 |       // on the next iteration.
112 |       DiGraphNode<N, E> source = workSet.iterator().next();
113 |       N sourceValue = source.getValue();
114 | 
115 |       workSet.remove(source);
116 | 
117 |       List<DiGraphEdge<N, E>> outEdges = source.getOutEdges();
118 |       for (DiGraphEdge<N, E> edge : outEdges) {
119 |         N destNode = edge.getDestination().getValue();
120 |         if (callback.traverseEdge(sourceValue, edge.getValue(), destNode)) {
121 |           workSet.add(edge.getDestination());
122 |         }
123 |       }
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     Preconditions.checkState(cycleCount != maxIterations,
127 |         NON_HALTING_ERROR_MSG);
128 |   }

===== M1370 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VarCheck.java
Original range: 126-213
Documentation:

Method code:
126 |   @Override
127 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
128 |     if (n.getType() != Token.NAME) {
129 |       return;
130 |     }
131 | 
132 |     String varName = n.getString();
133 | 
134 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
135 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
136 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunction(parent));
137 | 
138 |       // A function declaration with an empty name passes Rhino,
139 |       // but is supposed to be a syntax error according to the spec.
140 |       if (!NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
141 |         t.report(n, INVALID_FUNCTION_DECL);
142 |       }
143 |       return;
144 |     }
145 | 
146 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
147 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
148 |     if ((parent.getType() == Token.VAR ||
149 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
150 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
151 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
152 | 
153 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
154 |     }
155 | 
156 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
157 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
158 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
159 |     if (var == null) {
160 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
161 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
162 |         // current scope.
163 |       } else {
164 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
165 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
166 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
167 |         }
168 | 
169 |         if (sanityCheck) {
170 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
171 |         } else {
172 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
173 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
174 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
175 |         }
176 |       }
177 |       return;
178 |     }
179 | 
180 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
181 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
182 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
183 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
184 |       return;
185 |     }
186 | 
187 |     // Check module dependencies.
188 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
189 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
190 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
191 |     if (varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
192 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
193 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
194 |       } else {
195 |         if (!sanityCheck && scope.isGlobal()) {
196 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
197 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
198 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |           } else {
201 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
202 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
203 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
204 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
205 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
206 |           }
207 |         } else {
208 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
209 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
210 |         }
211 |       }
212 |     }
213 |   }

/**
     * Processes the parent of a GETPROP prototype, which can either be
     * another GETPROP (in the case of Foo.prototype.bar), or can be
     * an assignment (in the case of Foo.prototype = ...).
     */
Method code:
230 |     private void processPrototypeParent(NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
231 |       switch (n.getType()) {
232 |         // Foo.prototype.getBar = function() { ... } or
233 |         // Foo.prototype.getBar = getBaz (where getBaz is a function)
234 |         // parse tree looks like:
235 |         // assign                          <- parent
236 |         //     getprop                     <- n
237 |         //         getprop

239 |         //             string prototype

745 |     @Override
746 |     Node processObjectLiteral(ObjectLiteral literalNode) {
747 |       if (literalNode.isDestructuring()) {
748 |         reportDestructuringAssign(literalNode);
749 |       }

751 |       Node node = newNode(Token.OBJECTLIT);
752 |       for (ObjectProperty el : literalNode.getElements()) {
753 |         if (config.languageMode == LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT3) {
754 |           if (el.isGetter()) {

Original range: 1714-1777

/**
   * @param compareJsType Whether to compare the JSTypes of the nodes.
   * @param recurse Whether to compare the children of the current node, if
   *    not only the the count of the children are compared.
   * @return Whether this node is equivalent semantically to the provided node.
   */
Method code:
1714 |   boolean isEquivalentTo(Node node, boolean compareJsType, boolean recurse) {
1715 |     if (type != node.getType()
1716 |         || getChildCount() != node.getChildCount()
1717 |         || getNodeClass(this) != getNodeClass(node)) {
1718 |       return false;
1719 |     }
1720 | 
1721 |     if (compareJsType && !JSType.isEquivalent(jsType, node.getJSType())) {
1722 |       return false;
1723 |     }
1724 | 
1725 |     if (type == Token.ARRAYLIT) {
1726 |       try {
1727 |         int[] indices1 = (int[]) getProp(Node.SKIP_INDEXES_PROP);
1728 |         int[] indices2 = (int[]) node.getProp(Node.SKIP_INDEXES_PROP);
1729 |         if (indices1 == null) {
1730 |           if (indices2 != null) {
1731 |             return false;
1732 |           }
1733 |         } else if (indices2 == null) {
1734 |           return false;
1735 |         } else if (indices1.length != indices2.length) {
1736 |           return false;
1737 |         } else {
1738 |           for (int i = 0; i < indices1.length; i++) {
1739 |             if (indices1[i] != indices2[i]) {
1740 |               return false;
1741 |             }
1742 |           }
1743 |         }
1744 |       } catch (Exception e) {
1745 |         return false;
1746 |       }
1747 |     } else if (type == Token.INC || type == Token.DEC) {
1748 |       int post1 = this.getIntProp(INCRDECR_PROP);
1749 |       int post2 = node.getIntProp(INCRDECR_PROP);
1750 |       if (post1 != post2) {
1751 |         return false;
1752 |       }
1753 |     } else if (type == Token.STRING) {
1754 |       int quoted1 = this.getIntProp(QUOTED_PROP);
1755 |       int quoted2 = node.getIntProp(QUOTED_PROP);
1756 |       if (quoted1 != quoted2) {
1757 |         return false;
1758 |       }
1759 |     } else if (type == Token.CALL) {
1760 |       if (this.getBooleanProp(FREE_CALL) != node.getBooleanProp(FREE_CALL)) {
1761 |         return false;
1762 |       }
1763 |     }
1764 | 
1765 |     if (recurse) {
1766 |       Node n, n2;
1767 |       for (n = first, n2 = node.first;
1768 |            n != null;
1769 |            n = n.next, n2 = n2.next) {
1770 |         if (!n.isEquivalentTo(n2, compareJsType, true)) {
1771 |           return false;

1774 |     }

134 |   @Override
135 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
136 |     if (colorings.isEmpty() || !NodeUtil.isName(n) ||
137 |         NodeUtil.isFunction(parent)) {
138 |       // Don't rename named functions.
139 |       return;
140 |     }
141 |     Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
142 |     GraphNode<Var, ?> vNode = colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(var);
143 |     if (vNode == null) {
144 |       // This is not a local.
145 |       return;
146 |     }
147 |     Var coalescedVar = colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(var);
148 | 
149 |     if (!usePseudoNames) {
150 |       if (vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar)) {
151 |         // The coalesced name is itself, nothing to do.
152 |         return;
153 |       }
154 | 
155 |       // Rename.
156 |       n.setString(coalescedVar.name);
157 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
158 | 
159 |       if (NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
160 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
161 |       }
162 |     } else {
163 |       // This code block is slow but since usePseudoName is for debugging,
164 |       // we should not sacrifice performance for non-debugging compilation to
165 |       // make this fast.
166 |       String pseudoName = null;
167 |       Set<String> allMergedNames = Sets.newTreeSet();
168 |       for (Iterator<Var> i = t.getScope().getVars(); i.hasNext();) {
169 |         Var iVar = i.next();
170 | 
171 |         // Look for all the variables that can be merged (in the graph by now)
172 |         // and it is merged with the current coalscedVar.
173 |         if (colorings.peek().getGraph().getNode(iVar) != null &&
174 |             coalescedVar.equals(colorings.peek().getPartitionSuperNode(iVar))) {
175 |           allMergedNames.add(iVar.name);
176 |         }
177 |       }
178 | 
179 |       // Keep its original name.
180 |       if (allMergedNames.size() == 1) {
181 |         return;
182 |       }
183 | 
184 |       pseudoName = Joiner.on("_").join(allMergedNames);
185 | 
186 |       while (t.getScope().isDeclared(pseudoName, true)) {
187 |         pseudoName += "$";
188 |       }
189 | 
190 |       n.setString(pseudoName);
191 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
192 | 
193 |       if (!vNode.getValue().equals(coalescedVar) && NodeUtil.isVar(parent)) {
194 |         removeVarDeclaration(n);
195 |       }
196 |     }
197 |   }

===== M1438 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.referenceAliases()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NameAnalyzer.java
Original range: 1259-1268
Documentation:
/**
   * The NameAnalyzer algorithm works best when all objects have a canonical
   * name in the global scope. When multiple names in the global scope
   * point to the same object, things start to break down.
   *
   * For example, if we have
   * <code>
   * var a = {};
   * var b = a;
   * a.foo = 3;
   * alert(b.foo);
   * </code>
   * then a.foo and b.foo are the same name, even though NameAnalyzer doesn't
   * represent them as such.
   *
   * To handle this case, we look at all the aliases in the program.
   * If descendant properties of that alias are assigned, then we create a
   * directional reference from the original name to the alias. For example,
   * in this case, the assign to {@code a.foo} triggers a reference from
   * {@code b} to {@code a}, but NOT from a to b.
   *
   * Similarly, "instanceof" checks do not prevent the removal
   * of a unaliased name but an instanceof check on an alias can only be removed
   * if the other aliases are also removed, so we add a connection here.
   */
Method code:
1259 |   private void referenceAliases() {
1260 |     for (Map.Entry<String, AliasSet> entry : aliases.entrySet()) {
1261 |       JsName name = getName(entry.getKey(), false);
1262 |       if (name.hasWrittenDescendants || name.hasInstanceOfReference) {
1263 |         for (String alias : entry.getValue().names) {
1264 |           recordReference(alias, entry.getKey(), RefType.REGULAR);
1265 |         }
1266 |       }
1267 |     }
1268 |   }

/** Re-arrange the passes in an optimal order. */
Method code:
362 |     private void optimizePasses() {
363 |       // It's important that this ordering is deterministic, so that
364 |       // multiple compiles with the same input produce exactly the same
365 |       // results.
366 |       //
367 |       // To do this, grab any passes we recognize, and move them to the end

373 |             optimalPasses.add(pass);
374 |             break;
375 |           }
376 |         }
377 |       }
378 | 
379 |       myPasses.removeAll(optimalPasses);
380 |       myPasses.addAll(optimalPasses);
381 |     }

228 |     propsByFreq.addAll(propertyMap.values());
229 |     generateNames(propsByFreq, reservedNames);
230 | 
231 |     // Update the string nodes.
232 |     boolean changed = false;
233 |     for (Node n : stringNodesToRename) {
234 |       String oldName = n.getString();
235 |       Property p = propertyMap.get(oldName);
236 |       if (p != null && p.newName != null) {
237 |         Preconditions.checkState(oldName.equals(p.oldName));
238 |         n.setString(p.newName);
239 |         changed = changed || !p.newName.equals(oldName);
240 |       }
241 |     }
242 | 
243 |     // Update the call nodes.
244 |     for (Node n : callNodeToParentMap.keySet()) {
245 |       Node parent = callNodeToParentMap.get(n);
246 |       Node firstArg = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
247 |       StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
248 |       for (String oldName : firstArg.getString().split("[.]")) {
249 |         Property p = propertyMap.get(oldName);
250 |         String replacement;
251 |         if (p != null && p.newName != null) {
252 |           Preconditions.checkState(oldName.equals(p.oldName));
253 |           replacement = p.newName;
254 |         } else {
255 |           replacement = oldName;
256 |         }
257 |         if (sb.length() > 0) {
258 |           sb.append('.');
259 |         }
260 |         sb.append(replacement);
261 |       }
262 |       parent.replaceChild(n, Node.newString(sb.toString()));
263 |       changed = true;
264 |     }
265 | 
266 |     if (changed) {
267 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
268 |     }
269 | 
270 |     compiler.setLifeCycleStage(LifeCycleStage.NORMALIZED_OBFUSCATED);
271 |   }

Method code:
135 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
136 |       if (n.getType() == Token.VAR) {
137 |         blacklistStubVars(t, n);
138 |       }
139 | 
140 |       // Only care about var nodes
141 |       if (n.getType() != Token.VAR && !canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope())) return;
142 | 
143 |       // If we've already looked at this node, skip it
144 |       if (nodesToCollapse.contains(n)) return;
145 | 
146 |       // Adjacent VAR children of an IF node are the if and else parts and can't
147 |       // be collapsed
148 |       if (parent.getType() == Token.IF) return;
149 | 
150 |       Node varNode = n;
151 | 
152 |       boolean hasVar = n.getType() == Token.VAR;
153 | 
154 |       // Find variable declarations that follow this one (if any)
155 |       n = n.getNext();
156 | 
157 |       boolean hasNodesToCollapse = false;
158 | 
159 |       while (n != null &&
160 |           (n.getType() == Token.VAR || canBeRedeclared(n, t.getScope()))) {
161 | 
162 |         if (NodeUtil.isVar(n)) {
163 |           blacklistStubVars(t, n);
164 |           hasVar = true;
165 |         }
166 | 
167 |         nodesToCollapse.add(n);
168 |         hasNodesToCollapse = true;
169 | 
170 |         n = n.getNext();
171 |       }
172 | 
173 |       if (hasNodesToCollapse && hasVar) {
174 |         nodesToCollapse.add(varNode);
175 |         collapses.add(new Collapse(varNode, n, parent));
176 |       }
177 |     }

199 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {

203 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.MethodCompilerPass.GetExternMethods.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/MethodCompilerPass.java
Original range: 127-172
Documentation:

Method code:
127 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
128 |       switch (n.getType()) {
129 |         case Token.GETPROP:
130 |         case Token.GETELEM: {
131 |           Node dest = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
132 | 
133 |           if (dest.getType() != Token.STRING) {
134 |             return;
135 |           }
136 | 
137 |           String name = dest.getString();
138 | 
139 |           // We have a signature. Parse tree of the form:
140 |           // assign                       <- parent
141 |           //      getprop                 <- n
142 |           //          name methods
143 |           //          string setTimeout
144 |           //      function
145 |           if (parent.getType() == Token.ASSIGN &&
146 |               parent.getFirstChild() == n &&
147 |               n.getNext().getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
148 |             addSignature(name, n.getNext(), t.getSourceName());
149 |           } else {
150 |             getSignatureStore().removeSignature(name);
151 |             externMethodsWithoutSignatures.add(name);
152 |           }
153 | 
154 |           externMethods.add(name);
155 |         } break;
156 | 
157 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
158 |           for (Node key = n.getFirstChild(); key != null; key = key.getNext()) {
159 |             Node value = key.getFirstChild();
160 |             String name = key.getString();
161 |             if (key.getType() == Token.STRING
162 |                 && value.getType() == Token.FUNCTION) {
163 |               addSignature(name, value, t.getSourceName());
164 |             } else {
165 |               getSignatureStore().removeSignature(name);
166 |               externMethodsWithoutSignatures.add(name);
167 |             }
168 |             externMethods.add(name);
169 |           }
170 |         } break;
171 |       }
172 |     }

/**
     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of
     * Ecma-262, Edition 5.
     *

     * us, but right now their directive-processing is a one-off.

Method code:
448 |     private void parseDirectives(Node node) {

===== M1547 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeRemoveDeadCode.java
Original range: 169-279
Documentation:
/**
   * General cascading unused operation node removal.
   * @param n The root of the expression to simplify.
   * @param removeUnused If true, the node is removed from the AST if
   *     it is not useful, otherwise it replaced with an EMPTY node.
   * @return The replacement node, or null if the node was is not useful.
   */
Method code:
169 |   private Node trySimplifyUnusedResult(Node n, boolean removeUnused) {
170 |     Node result = n;
171 | 
172 |     // Simplify the results of conditional expressions
173 |     switch (n.getType()) {
174 |       case Token.HOOK:
175 |         Node trueNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild().getNext());
176 |         Node falseNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
177 |         // If one or more of the conditional children were removed,
178 |         // transform the HOOK to an equivalent operation:
179 |         //    x() ? foo() : 1 --> x() && foo()
180 |         //    x() ? 1 : foo() --> x() || foo()
181 |         //    x() ? 1 : 1 --> x()
182 |         //    x ? 1 : 1 --> null
183 |         if (trueNode == null && falseNode != null) {
184 |           n.setType(Token.OR);
185 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
186 |         } else if (trueNode != null && falseNode == null) {
187 |           n.setType(Token.AND);
188 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
189 |         } else if (trueNode == null && falseNode == null) {
190 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
191 |         } else {
192 |           // The structure didn't change.
193 |           result = n;
194 |         }
195 |         break;
196 |       case Token.AND:
197 |       case Token.OR:
198 |         // Try to remove the second operand from a AND or OR operations:
199 |         //    x() || f --> x()
200 |         //    x() && f --> x()
201 |         Node conditionalResultNode = trySimplifyUnusedResult(
202 |             n.getLastChild());
203 |         if (conditionalResultNode == null) {
204 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
205 |           // The conditionally executed code was removed, so
206 |           // replace the AND/OR with its LHS or remove it if it isn't useful.
207 |           result = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
208 |         }
209 |         break;
210 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
211 |         // A function expression isn't useful if it isn't used, remove it and
212 |         // don't bother to look at its children.
213 |         result = null;
214 |         break;
215 |       case Token.COMMA:
216 |         // We rewrite other operations as COMMA expressions (which will later
217 |         // get split into individual EXPR_RESULT statement, if possible), so
218 |         // we special case COMMA (we don't want to rewrite COMMAs as new COMMAs
219 |         // nodes.
220 |         Node left = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getFirstChild());
221 |         Node right = trySimplifyUnusedResult(n.getLastChild());
222 |         if (left == null && right == null) {
223 |           result = null;
224 |         } else if (left == null) {
225 |           result = right;
226 |         } else if (right == null){
227 |           result = left;
228 |         } else {
229 |           // The structure didn't change.
230 |           result = n;
231 |         }
232 |         break;
233 |       default:
234 |         if (!NodeUtil.nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects(n)) {
235 |           // This is the meat of this function. The node itself doesn't generate
236 |           // any side-effects but preserve any side-effects in the children.
237 |           Node resultList = null;
238 |           for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
239 |             next = c.getNext();
240 |             c = trySimplifyUnusedResult(c);
241 |             if (c != null) {
242 |               c.detachFromParent();
243 |               if (resultList == null)  {
244 |                 // The first side-effect can be used stand-alone.
245 |                 resultList = c;
246 |               } else {
247 |                 // Leave the side-effects in-place, simplifying it to a COMMA
248 |                 // expression.
249 |                 resultList = new Node(Token.COMMA, resultList, c)
250 |                     .copyInformationFrom(c);
251 |               }
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 |           result = resultList;
255 |         }
256 |     }
257 | 
258 |     // Fix up the AST, replace or remove the an unused node (if requested).
259 |     if (n != result) {
260 |       Node parent = n.getParent();
261 |       if (result == null) {
262 |         if (removeUnused) {
263 |           parent.removeChild(n);
264 |         } else {
265 |           result = new Node(Token.EMPTY).copyInformationFrom(n);
266 |           parent.replaceChild(n, result);
267 |         }
268 |       } else {
269 |         // A new COMMA expression may not have an existing parent.
270 |         if (result.getParent() != null) {
271 |           result.detachFromParent();
272 |         }
273 |         n.getParent().replaceChild(n, result);
274 |       }
275 |       reportCodeChange();
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     return result;
279 |   }
